The empirical study doesn't test capex/capacity directly (no capex_to_revenue or ppe_growth feature), but its closest proxies point the same 'necessary-but-insufficient' direction: winners show materially higher shares_growth_yoy (AUC 0.61, the single strongest feature in the 'all' cohort) — consistent with equity-funded capacity build-out — and lower ocf_ttm/gross_margin (AUC 0.41/0.41, winners burning more cash and running thinner margins), consistent with capex outrunning current revenue. None of the cited literature (R&D intensity, patent efficiency, organization capital, MAX effect) speaks to capex/capacity specifically, so literature is silent rather than confirming or contradicting.

Net: not refuted — the signal is real, cheap, and knowable in time, and the dilution/cash-burn proxies in the empirical study are directionally supportive. But it cannot stand as a 'core' discriminator because the graveyard evidence shows the identical fact pattern (capacity/plant/GPU buildout ahead of revenue) also describes companies that went to zero. Keep as a supporting feature only when paired with a binding-demand check (deposits/contracts/delivered units in subsequent filings, not press-release 'orders') and a disclosed-runway/burn-rate gate — exactly the discriminators this dataset flags as doing the actual separating work.

The family bundles two sub-signals of very different quality, and the case-study set itself is the evidence that they must be split, not averaged.

(1) Insider Form-4 buy/sell direction — actively contradicted by its own evidence. In the 14 instances supplied, insider selling or zero open-market buying preceded/accompanied the run in PLTR (Thiel/Karp heavy selling, explicitly logged as "pointed the wrong way," +150% followed anyway), SMCI (CEO Liang recurring sales incl. a $12.6M sale during the run itself), APLD (no meaningful insider buying in the 12mo setup window), QBTS (zero open-market buys, all sells/comp grants), and RKLB (CEO sold 3.6M shares, zero buys on record). A 13-Form-4 cluster on VRT that looked like coordinated insider conviction was opened and turned out to be $0.00-price compensation vesting, not conviction buying — a false positive caught by hand-checking, not by the screen. That is five-plus winners where the naive "insiders buy = bullish / insiders sell = bearish" read gives the wrong or a null answer, out of a small sample. This is exactly the graveyard doctrine's warning applied to a different signal: a metric that looks identical across outcomes has no discriminating power, and here it looks identical to a false signal even within winners alone — no graveyard-side comparison is provided at all, so I cannot confirm collapsed names show the same pattern, but the burden should sit on the signal, not the reviewer, and it hasn't been met.

(2) Institutional accumulation (13D activist stakes, 13F filer-count acceleration, ARK's daily disclosure) — the more genuinely supportive strand: APLD/Oasis 13D with board seat 13mo before the run, OKLO's 13F filer count going 1→91 in one quarter, TSLA/Baillie Gifford raising to ~7.7% during the depths of a scandal, ARK's same-day dip-buying disclosures on PLTR. But three of these four are confirming/momentum-adjacent rather than clearly leading (Baillie Gifford was already TSLA's largest outside holder; OKLO's 13F jump coincided with the de-SPAC merger closing, the news event itself; ARK's buys preceded an 8-month further drawdown before PLTR's actual run). Only the APLD/Oasis 13D reads as a clean, dated, leading, checkable discriminator.

(3) No empirical test exists for this family. The study's ten features (rev growth, R&D/rev, margins, runway, shares_growth_yoy, ocf, momentum, drawdown) contain nothing that measures insider transactions or 13F/13D ownership; the closest proxy, shares_growth_yoy, has the highest AUC in the whole battery (0.61) but that measures dilution/share-count growth from capital raises, not institutional ownership direction, so it is at best a loose, indirect echo and not a validated test of this family. No literature entry addresses insider or institutional-ownership signals either — the supplied literature list covers R&D/patents/org-capital/MAX-effect only.

(4) Lag and free-data profile are genuinely favorable where the signal is real: Form 4 files within 2 business days (SEC EDGAR, free, real-time), Schedule 13D within 10 days of crossing 5% (free), 13G annually/on threshold, 13F quarterly with a ~45-day lag (free but stalest). All are scriptable via EDGAR full-text search/XBRL across ~500 names per this repo's REST-first doctrine — no browser needed. ARK's daily feed is free and fastest but single-manager, not scalable to a 500-name universe.

Net: the family is knowable in time and free to compute at scale, so it clears the mechanical bars, but the dominant, most commonly cited sub-signal (insider buy/sell direction) is repeatedly wrong-signed or null in the very case studies meant to support it, and the stronger sub-signal (activist 13D / institutional-base acceleration) has only one clean leading example and zero empirical or graveyard-side validation. That combination — real contradicting case evidence for the common version, no empirical test, no cross-check against failures — is supporting at best, not core: use 13D-activist-stake and sudden 13F-filer-count jumps as a contextual confirming input, and explicitly discard bare insider Form-4 direction as a standalone bullish/bearish timing signal for pre-profit small caps in this cohort.

No search was run; this judgment rests only on the supplied case list, graveyard discriminators, literature list, and empirical AUC table, per the task's constraint.

(1) Survivorship — high risk, and the graveyard evidence directly undercuts this family as a standalone discriminator. The graveyard discriminators explicitly say narrative/press-release/announcement content is NOT what separated NKLA/RIDE/GOEV from survivors — "treat every order/pre-order/LOI as worthless until confirmed," "watch what a partner does with its OWN capital, not what it announces," "a short-seller report existing is not itself the discriminator." Nikola, Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, Romeo Power all had at least as much attention/narrative build-up (EV "revolution," GM tie-up, celebrity CEOs, "self-driving"/"AI" framing) as NVDA's 2015-16 "deep learning" reframe or VRT's 2023 "AI investment" line. The two look identical in real time; the graveyard record only diverged later on binding-contract veracity, disclosed runway, and governance — none of which "attention_and_narrative" as defined here captures. So this family, taken alone, is a textbook look-alike, not a discriminator.

(2) Look-ahead — mixed but mostly favorable on knowability, weak on usable lead time. Filing-language adoption (NVDA's FY2015 10-K "deep learning," VRT's Q1'23 8-K Ex-99.1) and analyst-rating divergences (RKLB Street-low target, PLTR Underweight-through-the-run, APLD target-price gaps) are knowable the instant the filing/report posts, zero reporting lag, fully backtestable off EDGAR timestamps and dated analyst-rating feeds. But several instances in the same case set are the run's proximate trigger itself, not an early warning: QBTS/Google-Willow (0 months lead), TSLA/ARK ($4k thesis, but the stock had already begun re-rating), PLTR/ChatGPT (a cohort-wide macro catalyst, explicitly flagged in the data itself as "not by itself evidence that picked PLTR specifically"). So roughly half these instances buy real lead time (9-20 months); the other half are contemporaneous with, or slightly lag, the move — which caps how much of this family functions as a genuine leading indicator versus a coincident tag.

(3) Free data — yes, comprehensively. Every instance in the case list cites a free source: SEC EDGAR full-text search (10-K/10-Q/8-K keyword hits for "AI"/"deep learning"/narrative-shift language), company IR press releases, free analyst-rating aggregators (TipRanks free tier, MarketBeat, Benzinga), Google Trends/news-volume for attention spikes. EDGAR full-text search in particular scales cleanly to ~500 names as a scripted keyword-frequency/first-mention scan — this is the one part of the family that is unambiguously "core-grade" on data feasibility alone.

(4) Literature/empirical fit — no direct evidence either way, which is itself informative. The empirical study never tested a narrative/attention/textual feature (its ten features are all financial: growth, margin, runway, shares, OCF, momentum, drawdown), so it neither confirms nor refutes this family. The supplied literature (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis R&D intensity, Hirshleifer patent efficiency, Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou organization capital, Cohen-Diether-Malloy innovation mismatch) is about capitalized R&D/patent/org-capital measures, not sentiment or narrative-attention — a different signal family entirely, so it doesn't transfer support here. The one directly relevant meta-finding supplied, McLean & Pontiff (2016), warns that published/well-known predictors decay 26-58% out-of-sample/post-publication — and narrative-chasing is about as publicized and crowded as a signal gets, reinforcing rather than easing the survivorship concern.

Net: not refuted outright (no data actively falsifies it as unknowable or contradicts its existence — it's genuinely observable, cheaply, at scale, with real lead time in a subset of cases), but the graveyard record shows it is not a discriminator when used alone, since failed names generated the same kind of narrative signal. Keep as supporting: a free, scriptable, real-time lead-generation trigger (flag the EDGAR first-mention, the earnings-call reframe, the analyst-target gap) that must be paired with the graveyard's actual discriminators — binding-contract veracity, disclosed cash runway, governance/insider behavior — before it says anything about winner-vs-failure. Do not score or weight it as a standalone predictive feature; do use it to decide which names get the deeper filing-level check.

(1) Survivorship — fails as a standalone binary. The graveyard discriminators explicitly warn that dilutive financing/ATM programs/going-concern language appear in BOTH cohorts: Lordstown's boilerplate going-concern 10-K, Canoo's disclosed sub-quarter runway, and Luminar's ATM-dependent liquidity footnote are graveyard cases, yet the winner set in this brief itself contains financing events graded as distress-quality by the evidence's own annotation — RGTI's 11%/Prime+7.5% Trinity Capital venture debt ('a signal of an expensive-capital, cash-constrained balance sheet'), APLD's 9% Series E-1 preferred ('a fundamentals red flag rather than a bullish tell'), and QBTS's PSP loan (framed contemporaneously as a distress 'lifeline'). So the raw event class — a company raising dilutive/high-cost capital — is shared by eventual winners and eventual failures; it is not self-discriminating. What the graveyard notes actually isolate as separating is financing SUBTYPE and quality: strategic/informed-money equity at or near market (Nvidia→NBIS, Macquarie→APLD, AT&T/Google/Vodafone→ASTS, note-hedge-covered TSLA convert) versus forced, high-cost, covenant-heavy distress paper (RGTI's secured venture debt, APLD's 9% preferred, QBTS's IP-pledged loan) — plus post-raise behavior (did the money fund a real, later-vindicated buildout, or just extend a burn). That decomposition is not present in the raw family as stated, so survivorship_risk is high for the family taken at face value. (2) Look-ahead — clean. Every instance here is sourced to an 8-K/424B/10-Q/6-K, each with statutory filing deadlines (8-K: 4 business days of the event) that land 3-21 months before the subsequent run in this dataset (median ~9 months), so there is no look-ahead problem; the signal is knowable with a short, filing-driven lag well ahead of the price move. (3) Free data — yes. SEC EDGAR full-text search (8-K Item 1.01/3.02, 424B5, 10-Q/10-K liquidity footnotes, going-concern language) and XBRL frames (shares outstanding, common shares issued) are free and scriptable across the full ~500-name universe; Form 4 and press releases add named-investor identification for the strategic-vs-distress split. This matches the repo's own REST-first doctrine (CLAUDE.md §1.2) — no Playwright needed. (4) Literature/empirical — the supplied academic literature (R&D intensity, patent efficiency, organization capital, MAX effect) does not address financing/dilution directly, so it neither confirms nor contradicts. The empirical study, however, points the same direction as the qualitative cases: shares_growth_yoy has the single highest AUC of any feature tested (0.61 all-sample, 0.59 in tech_small, n=202/227 — the largest sample of any feature), meaning winners diluted MORE than industry-matched controls, not less — consistent with ENPH/TSLA/NBIS/APLD/CRWV all raising material capital shortly before their inflection. This sits alongside gross_margin (0.41), ocf_ttm (0.41), momentum (0.39/0.39) and drawdown_3y (0.33) all below 0.5, i.e., winners were lower-margin, cash-burning, and MORE beaten-down pre-run than controls — a coherent 'distressed-looking-but-funded' profile in which raising capital (the ability to keep diluting rather than dying) is the mechanism that buys the runway to the inflection, not an incidental correlate. Given (a) real, above-noise empirical separation (highest AUC in the study) and directional alignment with every case study, but (b) explicit within-dataset evidence that the same raw event also marks graveyard names and even some low-quality tranches inside the winner set itself, this belongs as a supporting signal — best used decomposed by counterparty quality/cost-of-capital and paired with the runway/burn and drawdown features it correlates with — rather than a standalone core discriminator.

(1) Survivorship: fails the key test. The graveyard set (NKLA, RIDE, HYLN) attracted heavy short interest and short-seller reports too — the graveyard notes explicitly say a short-seller report/attention "is NOT itself the discriminator" between collapses and survivors. So the specific instances offered (AMD ~25% SI at $2, TSLA ~23% SI pre-Q3-2019, VRT/APLD/IONQ/QBTS crowded shorts, IREN moderate SI at cycle low) describe a condition — extreme two-sided positioning on a beaten-down, controversial name — that shows up in both eventual 5x winners and eventual zero-outcome frauds/failures. By itself this is not a directional discriminator; it's an amplifier/attention signal that needs a real catalyst (AMD's actual turnaround, VRT's actual beats) to resolve bullish rather than to zero. PLTR (not crowded) and ENPH/NBIS/SOUN (not short-interest signals at all, just price-anomaly/valuation snapshots) further show this "family" is a loose grab-bag rather than one clean mechanism.
(2) Look-ahead: clean. FINRA short interest is reported bi-monthly and is a live, contemporaneous number (weeks of lag, not restated later); 10-K cover-page market values and relisting prices are point-in-time SEC/exchange facts. No hindsight contamination — fully knowable at the time with short, known lag.
(3) Free data: yes, comprehensively — FINRA.org bi-monthly short-interest files and Nasdaq/exchange short-interest pages are free and cover essentially the full US-listed universe, so this scales to ~500 names with no vendor gate. SEC EDGAR full-text/XBRL covers the 10-K market-value and relisting-price cases.
(4) Literature vs. empirical study: the classical short-interest literature (Asquith-Pathak-Ritter, Boehme-Danielsen-Sorescu; not directly re-verified this session but not contradicted by anything opened) finds elevated short interest on average predicts *lower*, not higher, future returns — the opposite sign from the "squeeze fuels the run" narrative used in half these case studies, and this family isn't even one of the literature items supplied (R&D intensity, patents, org capital, MAX effect) — no literature-side corroboration was actually verified. The empirical study never tests short interest directly, but its closest proxies point the same beaten-down direction as the case studies: mom_6m_pre/mom_12m_pre AUC 0.39/0.39 and drawdown_3y AUC 0.33 (all <0.5) show winners were *more* beaten-down/lower-momentum than matched controls at run-start-minus-3mo — consistent with "high-short/hated-name" positioning preceding the multibagger run, but this is circumstantial, not a direct AUC on short interest itself.
Net: knowable-in-time and free-data conditions are both satisfied, so this isn't unknowable or refuted outright, but the graveyard evidence directly undercuts using extreme short interest as a standalone discriminator — it's a crowding/context flag (flags volatility/amplification potential once a catalyst hits) that must be paired with a fundamental or catalyst signal, not a core screen on its own.

(1) Survivorship: The graveyard section is directly on-point for this exact family and is damning by omission — it names "order," "pre-order," and "letter of intent" announcements as the single most common false-positive mechanism across the collapsed cohort (NKLA-GM, GOEV-Walmart/Kingbee/Zeeba, RIDE's 100k "pre-orders" traced to shell entities paid $30-50 each). A naive "supply_chain_link exists" screen would have scored Nikola's GM tie-up and GOEV's retail deals identically to AMD's wafer agreement at announcement time; only ex-post facts (deposit, no termination clause, delivered units in subsequent 10-Qs, or independent corroboration) separated them. Of the four instances supplied, three are less exposed to that failure mode because they carry independent corroboration rather than bare press-release terms: AMD's Sixth Amendment involved AMD paying GF $100M in cash installments (a real liability, not a promise); IREN's power/land claims are cross-checkable against FERC/ERCOT interconnection-queue filings, a third party outside the company's control; SMCI's claim is a self-reported product-mix shift (server/storage rising to 85.9% of sales) that is verifiable in later filings rather than a named-customer order. SOUN's is a decade-old shipped, revenue-generating OEM relationship, the opposite of a hollow LOI. None of the four is a pure unconfirmed "order announcement," but the family as titled ("supply_chain_link") does not itself encode the binding/delivered distinction, so a mechanical screen built on the label alone would re-admit the Nikola/GOEV failure pattern. That gap, not the four cherry-picked instances, is the survivorship concern.
(2) Look-ahead: Knowable at the time with short, mechanical lag — 8-K/6-K within ~1-4 business days of the event, 10-K/10-Q on the standard quarterly/annual cadence, all timestamped on EDGAR. However lead time is wildly inconsistent within the family itself: AMD's own instance is explicitly flagged by the source as a mid-run confirmation (months_before_run = -8, i.e., 8 months into the run, not a leading indicator), while SOUN's is 60 months out (arguably too early/generic to be an actionable "signal" for a specific run) and SMCI/IREN sit in a plausible 6-14 month pre-run window. A family whose own best example is labeled non-leading is a caution flag on the family's leading-indicator claim, not a confirmation of it.
(3) Free data: Yes — SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) and XBRL cover 8-K/10-K/6-K material-contract exhibits at zero cost and are scriptable across ~500 tickers (per this repo's own REST-first doctrine); FERC/ERCOT interconnection queues and USAspending are free cross-checks for the infra-buildout sub-case. Extracting "is there a supply/customer/capacity disclosure" via keyword search (full-text search API) is cheap; extracting whether that disclosure is *binding* (deposit, termination clause, delivered units) requires reading contract exhibits and later 10-Qs — doable but not a one-shot keyword pull, i.e., free data exists but the higher-value part of this signal (bindingness) is labor-intensive to operationalize at scale.
(4) Literature/empirical study: neither weighs in either direction. None of the cited academic papers (R&D intensity, patent efficiency, organization capital, innovation mispricing) address supply-chain or customer-contract disclosures as a predictor, and the empirical study's feature set (revenue growth, margins, cash flow, momentum, drawdown, share growth) contains no supply-chain-link proxy — so there is no quantitative AUC evidence for or against this family from either source. Absence of empirical testing plus the graveyard's explicit warning that the raw signal is indistinguishable from the mechanism that produced several outright collapses means this cannot be called "core" (discriminating and validated); it is not refuted either, since it is knowable in time, free data exists, and the four instances given are not actually the hollow-LOI type the graveyard warns about. Net: keep as a supporting signal, gated hard behind the graveyard's binding/delivered-units check before it is trusted as a leading indicator, and treat AMD's own case as evidence this family often confirms mid-run rather than leading it.

The four instances offered as one family are actually three different things, and only one is a clean regulatory catalyst. (1) RGTI's DEF 14A reverse-split approval and its Nasdaq 5550(a)(2) minimum-bid deficiency notice are distress/compliance events, not policy tailwinds — a company disclosing it is near delisting. The graveyard discriminators explicitly warn that boilerplate/near-universal disclosures (going-concern language, in that list) are low-signal because failed names show the same thing; a reverse-split-to-avoid-delisting is the same category of near-universal microcap event, seen constantly in names that went to zero (Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, etc., per the same case set), so RGTI's occurrence of it before a subsequent rally is very plausibly survivorship bias — we're told about the delisting notice because RGTI happened to recover, not because the notice predicts recovery. (2) The OKLO/Three-Mile-Island item is mislabeled: Microsoft-Constellation's PPA is a private commercial contract, not a "policy_or_regulation" action by any agency, and it has 0 months of lead time — it lands at the run's start, so even if it were genuine policy, it has no early-warning value; it's coincident, not leading. (3) Only the ASTS FCC 'Supplemental Coverage from Space' NPRM is a genuine case: a dated federal agency rulemaking, disclosed in a 10-K risk-factor/MD&A cross-reference, with a real 13-month lead — this is the one instance that fits the family as named. Literature provided (R&D intensity, patent efficiency, organization capital, MAX effect, publication decay) says nothing about regulatory-catalyst timing, so it neither supports nor contradicts this family. The empirical study's feature set (rev growth, R&D/rev, margins, runway, shares growth, OCF, momentum, drawdown) has no matching feature for policy/regulatory catalysts, so the AUC table is silent here too — no empirical corroboration either way. Net: knowable in time via free sources (SEC EDGAR full-text/DEF14A/8-K search, FCC ECFS docket search, both free and scriptable across ~500 names) — so the infrastructure criterion passes — but the underlying construct as evidenced is a grab-bag where 2-3 of 4 examples are either indistinguishable from failure-company boilerplate or non-leading/mislabeled, and only one (sector-specific agency rulemaking disclosed in filings, e.g., FCC/NRC/FDA-type dated dockets) looks like a real discriminator. That single clean subtype is worth tracking as context alongside other signals, but the family as defined does not clear the bar for 'core' given high survivorship risk and zero corroboration from literature or the empirical study.

(1) Survivorship — untested here, and that's the real gap. Only two winner instances are given (APLD's COO hire, ASTS's patent+distribution moat); no collapsed-name comparison is supplied, and none of the graveyard discriminators actually list "hiring" or "patent claims" as something that separated survivors from collapses — the discriminators that fired were order-book veracity, governance concentration, disclosed runway, and post-setback capital allocation, a different category entirely. From general (unverified-this-session) knowledge, splashy senior-executive hires with large comp packages and broad "patent-pending" claims are common among failed hype-stage names too (Nikola brought in credentialed auto-industry executives; patent-pending filings are cheap and don't require novelty to be granted), so the raw observable plausibly does not discriminate — this is an inferred concern, not a verified one, which is exactly why survivorship risk is rated high rather than the family being refuted outright.

(2) Look-ahead — clean. Executive appointments are Item 5.02 8-Ks, legally due within 4 business days of the event (APLD: event 2024-11-27, filed 2024-12-04, consistent with that window); patent portfolios and commercial-framework agreements are continuously public via USPTO records and 8-K/S-1 exhibits. Effectively zero look-ahead lag either way.

(3) Free data — yes, at scale. SEC EDGAR full-text search can be swept for Item 5.02 8-Ks and DEF 14A comp tables across ~500 tickers via the free EDGAR FTS API; patent counts/citations are free via USPTO Patent Public Search or the free PatentsView API. No paywall blocks a ~500-name sweep.

(4) Literature vs. the empirical study point in different directions, and the study is the more relevant test here. The literature (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis on R&D intensity, Hirshleifer-Hsu-Li on patents-per-R&D-dollar, Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou on organization capital, Kogan et al. on patent-implied value) broadly reports positive excess returns for innovation/organizational-capital signals in general equity universes — though several of the exact effect sizes are flagged in the evidence as recalled-from-training rather than verified this session, and McLean-Pontiff's own finding (verified via CrossRef abstract) is that published anomalies of exactly this kind decay 26-58% out-of-sample/post-publication. More importantly, the empirical study's nearest available proxy for this family — rnd_to_rev — shows essentially no discrimination in the specific population the question asks about: AUC 0.54 (all names), but 0.46 (tech) and 0.48 (tech_small, n=31 vs 46) — both *below* 0.5, meaning winners were if anything slightly less R&D-intensive than matched controls in pre-profit small-cap tech. That directly undercuts the patent/innovation half of the family for exactly this population. The hiring half has no empirical proxy tested at all. Combined with the study's other findings that winners in this cohort look distressed and dilutive (shares_growth_yoy AUC 0.59-0.61, negative momentum, deep prior drawdown) rather than "professionalizing," the seasoned-COO-hire narrative sits in some tension with what the winner cohort actually looked like operationally.

Net: not refuted (no evidence actively contradicts it, and hiring is simply untested rather than shown wrong), but the family should not be weighted as a core screen — it's cheap to compute from free data and knowable in time, but the one empirical test available in this dataset for its patent/R&D half is a coin-flip-or-worse in the target population, and the hiring half rests on an n=2 case-study base with no failure-side check. Treat as supporting color (part of a qualitative "is this company professionalizing / does it have a real IP-plus-distribution moat" read alongside filings) rather than a quantitative core signal.

refuted.name: other
refuted.reason: "Other" is not one testable signal but a grab-bag of narrative/governance facts (pre-existing profitability structure, leadership-change pivots, governance-overhang removal, clean-shell creation via divestiture, cash-vs-market-cap coverage, same-story competitor benchmarking). Verified this session via WebFetch: NBIS cash was $2,449.6M at 2024-12-31 against ~235.75M shares (SEC EX-99.1, confirms the dossier's cash figure and rough cash/mcap magnitude), and RGTI's Feb-2023 delisting/93% valuation collapse from its ~$1.5B SPAC value is accurately reported (thequantuminsider.com). Those two spot-checks hold up, but they don't rescue the family: the dossier's OWN instance list tags RGTI and ARQQ as explicit FALSE POSITIVES — same-vintage quantum SPACs chasing the identical narrative that IONQ rode, one delisted-near, one sued for securities fraud — and separately shows Intel/Nervana chasing NVDA's exact 'AI datacenter chip' story without a comparable re-rating. That is active, built-in contradicting evidence that narrative pattern-matching does not separate winners from failures; it's present on both sides. The one cleanly quantifiable piece here — cash covering a large % of market cap (NBIS) — is likewise undermined: the graveyard discriminators explicitly warn that large post-SPAC cash piles (Nikola, Lordstown, Canoo, all cited in the same dossier) are 'a number, not a vibe' and were present in names that still went to zero; what matters is cash vs. disclosed burn, and the empirical study's closest proxy for that, runway_years, shows AUC 0.48 (all) / 0.53 (tech) — essentially coin-flip, not discriminating. No literature entry supplied (R&D intensity, patents, org capital, MAX effect, decay) speaks to narrative-pivot, clean-shell, or cash-coverage signals at all, so there's no independent literature support either. Individually the underlying facts are true and dated (8-K leadership changes, 6-K/20-F cash and divestiture disclosures are knowable within days-to-months via free SEC EDGAR/XBRL/press), so this isn't a look-ahead or free-data problem — it fails on discrimination, not on knowability or cost.

backtest_protocol: Universe & vintage matching (avoids the retrospective-winners-only trap in the brief): build a POINT-IN-TIME list per historical date T using only SEC EDGAR data accepted on or before T — SIC codes for the three sectors + XBRL NetIncomeLoss<0 filter (scripts/aiinvest/universe.py, new). Include BOTH eventual winners (small-cap-vintage instances of NVDA/VRT/IONQ/RGTI/QBTS/ASTS/NBIS/APLD/IREN/CRWV/RKLB) AND the graveyard cohort (NKLA, RIDE, GOEV, Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, Hyliion, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Momentus, Velodyne, Luminar, MicroVision, BigBear.ai, QuantumScape, RGTI/ARQQ-as-false-positive instances) matched by sector, listing-vintage year, and market-cap decile at T -- never by 'known outcome', since the winner list in the brief was itself built retrospectively and has no failed-name counterexample for several sub-families (explicitly flagged for revenue_inflection and capex_or_capacity).

Freeze the model before touching any test era (edge-detection-method.md §2): fit gate thresholds and any scoring weights once on a designated train slice, persist the parameters to a versioned file, and treat any refit as an explicit, rare, logged action. Re-run the same test window with a 3-year vs a 15+ year training window and report both -- a result that swings sharply between them is regime-fitted, not structural (the method's own gold-regime example moved Sharpe 1.48 -> 0.31 on this exact test).

Count independent EVENTS, not filing-rows (§4): cluster every filing that documents the same underlying fact (e.g., three 10-Qs all showing one compressing-runway episode, or a going-concern paragraph repeated across consecutive quarters) into one event before any significance test. Use a moving-block bootstrap with block length set from the measured dependence length of the cluster (not the horizon), per §4a, when testing whether gate-tripped names differ from non-tripped names in eventual outcome.

Leakage avoidance, concretely: (a) every gate/signal value used to score date T must be computed only from filings with an EDGAR accepted-date <= T -- no using a later 10-K's restated numbers or a later-confirmed 'delivered units' fact to backfill an earlier binding-demand check; (b) sector/SIC classification used for universe construction must be the classification on file at T, not a present-day re-classification; (c) the 'sector leader' outcome label (the target being predicted) must be defined and locked BEFORE looking at any candidate's later price action, with a fixed lookback horizon (e.g., 24 months) -- otherwise the label itself becomes a garden-of-forking-paths free parameter.

Gate 1 -- Separation: for every gate/signal in the design (not a favorable subset), bootstrap the difference in eventual-outcome rate between gate-tripped and non-tripped cohorts and control the false-discovery rate across the whole set (BH-FDR) before calling any single gate 'validated'.

Gate 2 -- Fast detection: for each signal, measure l* = lag between (i) the date the signal was computable causally from filed data and (ii) the date the eventual outcome (re-rating or failure) became apparent with hindsight. Require l* < the locked outcome horizon; a signal only visible after the fact (as several case-study instances in the brief already are -- QBTS/Google-Willow at 0 months lead, several PLTR instances at ~2 months) fails this gate and must be demoted to a coincident/confirming tag, not a leading signal.

Gate 3 -- Edge survival: compute rho = (separation using only the causal, point-in-time score) / (separation using the full-hindsight-labeled version of the same score). Require rho >= 0.7; below 0.5 means the apparent edge is mostly hindsight -- exactly the failure mode the brief's own case list shows for narrative/attention and bare insider-direction sub-signals.

Era test (§5): split the point-in-time universe into at least 4 eras spanning distinct market regimes -- pre-2019, 2019-2021 SPAC/zero-rate boom, 2022-2023 rate-hike bust, 2024-2025 AI-infra boom -- train gates/weights on one era, test on an era the fit never saw, and report each era separately rather than one pooled number; a good pooled Sharpe/AUC with one dead era is a different (weaker) claim than steady performance.

Only after all three gates and the era test: apply 'costs' analogues appropriate to a research/screening tool rather than a trading strategy -- small-cap bid-ask spread and borrow-cost-if-shorting the graveyard cohort, EDGAR/FINRA data-lag realism (13F 45-day lag, FINRA short-interest 7-business-day lag), and an explicit statement that this system places no orders and is not sized as a portfolio (CLAUDE.md §11 -- no live account/order logic is in scope).

Record the number of variants tried at every stage (gate thresholds swept, weightings compared, label-horizon choices tested) -- per §8, that count is the denominator of any claim of significance, and an adversarial reviewer (a Sonnet sub-agent per CLAUDE.md's subagent model policy) should be handed the code and asked to find look-ahead paths and undercounted multiple-testing before any gate is called validated.
proposals.expected_base_rate_and_payoff: Verified-this-session base rates (Ritter's IPO long-run-return tables, opened directly, and the deSPAC literature cited in the dossier) put this exact population -- unprofitable-at-issue small caps -- at a 3-year market-adjusted buy-and-hold of roughly -30.7% on average (median across all IPOs even worse, -25.7%), with only ~7.7% of IPOs generally exceeding +200% over 3 years and ~1.7% exceeding +500%; deSPAC mergers (a disproportionate share of this exact sector population) average -57.7% market-adjusted over 3 years. "Sector leader" is a narrower, harder target than "any big winner," so the true hit rate for this system's target event is almost certainly below that already-thin 1.7-7.7% tail. Today's empirical study on this repo's own candidate feature set found AUC 0.48-0.55 for the standard fundamentals (revenue growth/acceleration) in exactly the tech-small-cap subgroup that matters -- statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip -- and the brief's core_families list is empty: no signal family cleared the "core, validated" bar this session. Net expectation: the system's honest current value is disqualification (screening OUT graveyard-pattern names via the verified graveyard discriminators -- going-concern language, hollow orders, governance capture, runway compression, exchange-compliance notices) rather than positive selection of the eventual leader; the payoff shape for whatever thin cohort survives all gates remains extremely right-skewed (a small minority of huge winners funding the return, consistent with Bessembinder's top-4%-of-all-stocks finding), so any probability the judge reports must be a wide, low band with heavy abstention, never a confident point estimate, until the backtest protocol above actually clears its three gates on point-in-time data.
build_plan_first_two_weeks: Day 1-2: superpowers:brainstorming already satisfied by this design pass; lock the target label definition (what counts as 'became a sector leader', fixed horizon e.g. 24 months) and the excluded/refuted signals list BEFORE writing any code, per CLAUDE.md §1 and edge-detection-method.md's order-of-operations.

Day 2-4: scripts/aiinvest/universe.py (new) -- point-in-time universe builder over SEC EDGAR SIC codes + XBRL companyfacts NetIncomeLoss, producing a dated snapshot per historical T; TDD (superpowers:test-driven-development) against 2-3 known dated cases (e.g. Canoo's SIC/financials as of a specific 10-Q date) to prove no lookahead leaks in.

Day 3-6: scripts/aiinvest/gates.py (new) implementing the graveyard-derived disqualifying gates as pure functions over already-fetched filings: going_concern_flag, governance_concentration_flag, binding_demand_check (cross-references an announced order/LOI against a LATER 10-Q's delivered-units/revenue line), runway_compression_rate, exchange_compliance_flag (NT 10-K/20-F, Item 3.01 8-K), exec_departure_funding_gap_flag. Each gets a unit test asserting it fires on the correct historical filing date for a known graveyard case (Canoo runway disclosure, Lordstown CEO/CFO departure, Virgin Orbit's 5Q->2Q runway compression) and does NOT fire earlier than the filing that actually disclosed it.

Day 4-6 (parallel via superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents, each Sonnet sub-agent, REST-first per CLAUDE.md §1.2): scripts/aiinvest/form4.py (new -- Form-4 transaction parser off data.sec.gov submissions, filling the data_gap the dossier already flagged) and reuse/extend scripts/aiinvest/tradingview.py + fundamental.py for the one empirically-nontrivial continuous feature, shares_growth_yoy (AUC 0.61 -- the single strongest tested feature), decomposed where possible by financing counterparty (strategic vs. distress) using 8-K Item 1.01/424B5 text.

Day 7-8: scripts/aiinvest/scorer.py (new) -- the deterministic, evidence-first scorer: any tripped disqualifying gate caps the score at a 'red-flag/avoid' band regardless of supporting signals; supporting signals (shares_growth_yoy, margin/OCF/momentum/drawdown ensemble, verified-binding anchor-customer, 13D activist stake) are combined only as a low-weight ensemble with weights capped by their measured AUC, never presented as high-confidence. Every score carries retrieved_at + source per filing (CLAUDE.md §1.3).

Day 8-10: scripts/aiinvest/backtest/ harness implementing the protocol above -- point-in-time replay, event clustering (§4), block bootstrap, the three gates, era splits. Run it first against the graveyard+winner case list already in the dossier as a smoke test before scaling to the ~500-name universe.

Day 10-12: the judge agent itself, wired as a Sonnet sub-agent (subagent-model-policy memory; CLAUDE.md §1.7) that consumes the scorer's output + gate flags + provenance and produces the narrative band/three-reasons/abstain-or-cite output defined below -- never touching the numeric score.

Day 12-13: superpowers:verification-before-completion -- run the full pipeline on 10-15 real names spanning both cohorts and show actual gate outputs + timestamps + judge narrative, not an assertion that it works.

Day 13-14: superpowers:requesting-code-review / an adversarial Sonnet sub-agent pass specifically hunting look-ahead paths, undercounted multiple-testing, and label-definition drift (§8); record the number of variants tried before calling anything validated.

inputs: The deterministic scorer's numeric output and every gate flag it tripped/did not trip (from scripts/aiinvest/scorer.py + gates.py), each tagged with its filing source, exact endpoint/URL, source_class, and retrieved_at per CLAUDE.md §1.3

The supporting-signal ensemble values (shares_growth_yoy, margin/OCF/momentum/drawdown, verified-binding anchor-customer flag, 13D activist-stake flag) with their measured AUC/weight and the population (all / tech / tech_small) that AUC was measured on
The base-rate table (Ritter IPO/deSPAC stats, MAX-effect, Bessembinder top-4%) so the judge's narrative is anchored to a documented prior rather than an implicit assumption of edge
XBRL/data-coverage completeness for the name (the ~45% coverage caveat) so the judge can decide whether to abstain on thin data
The case-study library of graveyard vs. winner discriminators from references/edge-detection-method.md and this brief, for pattern-matching context only -- never as a source of new numeric weight
judge_agent.outputs: A calibrated probability BAND (never a point estimate) drawn from a small fixed set (e.g. Insufficient-data/Abstain, Elevated-risk/Avoid-pattern-match, Watch-thin-evidence, Watch-favorable-but-unvalidated) chosen to match the near-coin-flip AUCs actually measured; exactly three reasons, each a one-sentence claim with an inline citation (filing URL + retrieved_at, or 'reported/rumored' tag if it is news-derived); the full list of tripped/untripped gates; an explicit abstain flag when required inputs are missing or stale; and a one-line reminder that this is educational research, not investment advice, and that no order was or will be placed on it.
rubric: Check every disqualifying gate FIRST. If any hard gate is tripped (going-concern language, unverified/hollow order-book, governance self-installation, compressing sub-2-quarter runway, exchange-compliance notice, funding-gap-tied executive departure), the output band is capped at Elevated-risk/Avoid regardless of any positive supporting signal -- mirrors the graveyard discriminators, which is the only category of evidence in this dossier with real case-level separating power.

Never adjust, re-weight, or override the deterministic scorer's numeric output. The judge's job is to explain and flag, not to compute a different number -- if the judge disagrees with the score, it says so as a flagged caveat in the reasons, not as a silent override.

Require a citable filing/source + retrieved_at for every factual claim placed in a 'reason'. If a claim cannot be traced to an opened primary source, either drop it or explicitly label it 'reported/rumored -- not independently verified this session'.

If XBRL/filing coverage for the name falls below the ~45% threshold documented in the empirical study, or a required gate cannot be computed (e.g. no 10-Q since the flagged announcement to check binding-demand), output Insufficient-data/Abstain rather than filling the gap with judgment.

Explicitly flag survivorship-bias-prone structures (post-SPAC, pre-revenue de-SPAC, single-customer-concentration) as a caveat in the output even when no hard gate trips, since the dossier shows these structures share surface signals with both winners and failures.

Separate every claim into filed (SEC/exchange primary source) vs. reported (news/press) vs. rumored (unconfirmed) and label accordingly in the output -- never launder a rumored deal or valuation into a filed fact.

State the AUC/n of any supporting signal cited in a reason, so a reader can see the confidence band the claim actually carries (e.g. 'higher shares_growth_yoy, AUC 0.61 on n=202/227 all-sample but only 0.59 on tech_small n=51/79') rather than presenting it as a strong predictor.
guardrails: Educational/research framing only in every output -- never phrase a band or reason as a buy/sell/hold recommendation; end every output with a not-investment-advice line.

Cite or abstain: any factual claim without an opened, dated primary source is either dropped or explicitly tagged unverified; the judge may not assert something as fact that this session did not verify.
Abstain on thin data rather than guessing: missing gate inputs, <45% filing coverage, or a stale (>1 filing-cycle-old) pull forces Insufficient-data/Abstain, not a best-guess band.

No override authority over the deterministic score -- the judge is a narrator and flagger, structurally separate from the scorer, so a persuasive-sounding narrative can never inflate or deflate the number.
No IBKR/brokerage account data ever enters this pipeline (CLAUDE.md §11) -- all inputs are public-filing/market-data sourced; nothing here reads or references any personal account.
Rumor/fact labeling is mandatory on every claim sourced from news rather than a filing, per CLAUDE.md §1.5.

proposals.name: Bumper Radar — Evidence-First Pre-Rerating Screener for Pre-Profit Emerging-Sector Small Caps
risks: Survivorship bias is structural, not incidental: the brief's own winner list (NVDA, VRT, PLTR, CRWV, NBIS, APLD, IONQ, RGTI, QBTS, ASTS, RKLB, IREN, SOUN, ENPH, TSLA, SMCI, AMD) was assembled retrospectively from known successes, and several sub-families (revenue_inflection, capex_or_capacity) have NO failed-name counterexample supplied to test against -- the system can look validated purely because it was never shown the graveyard case that shares the same surface pattern.

The one directly relevant empirical test available (today's 636-name AUC study) shows financial-statement features are near-coin-flip (AUC 0.48-0.55) in exactly the tech-small-cap population this system targets -- meaning the honest prior is that a purely-fundamentals score has little-to-no edge, and any apparent backtest lift must survive the three-gate test before being trusted rather than attributed to a real discriminator.

Thin independent-event counts: once filings are clustered into events (per §4 of the method) rather than counted as rows, the effective sample size for any gate's significance test could shrink to single digits per era, especially for rarer gates (governance self-installation, activist 13D) -- a result that looks significant on rows may not survive event-level, block-bootstrapped testing.

Label/target drift (garden of forking paths): 'became a sector leader' is not a standard, pre-existing label; if it is defined or adjusted after seeing which names would validate the system, every downstream gate and backtest number is contaminated by hindsight even if individual filing dates are correctly point-in-time.

Publication/decay risk (McLean & Pontiff, verified via CrossRef abstract this session): any signal that does show separation is likely to decay once it is systematized and used repeatedly, especially the narrative/attention and financing-quality sub-signals that are already widely discussed in retail/fintwit circles.

Data coverage gaps cap real-world usefulness: XBRL coverage is only ~45% for this population, no free near-real-time institutional-ownership or short-interest source exists (13F is 45 days stale, FINRA short interest is bi-monthly), and the highest-value discriminator the graveyard data names (bindingness of a contract) requires reading exhibit-level filing text, not a clean numeric field -- so full automation at scale is partial, and the system will abstain often by design.

Judge-agent narrative risk: an LLM asked to explain three reasons for a low-probability, high-uncertainty band is structurally tempted to write a more confident-sounding story than the underlying AUCs support (narrative smoothing) -- the rubric's citation-or-abstain and no-override rules mitigate but do not eliminate this; an adversarial review pass should specifically probe for this.

Legal/ToS and rate-limit risk at scale: EDGAR full-text search and XBRL frames are free but rate-limited (10 req/s, descriptive User-Agent required); FINRA short-interest data requires a free login and is restricted to non-commercial use; scaling gate computation across ~500 names must respect these, per CLAUDE.md §8.

Misuse risk: even with every guardrail, a probability band framed around 'sector leader' is easy to mistake for a stock tip; the deliverable must repeatedly and explicitly state it is educational/research only, not advice, and that this repo places no orders (CLAUDE.md §11.1).

signals.name: Going-concern / material-weakness language (hard gate)
signals.weight_or_role: Disqualifying gate — any hit caps the score at the lowest band regardless of other signals
signals.computation: EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) on the ticker/CIK for 'going concern' / 'material weakness' co-occurring with the filer; confirm via the specific 10-K/10-Q paragraph, dated to the filing's accepted date
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search API + XBRL companyfacts (free, no auth)
signals.why: One of the most repeatedly verified graveyard discriminators across every case cluster in the brief (Lordstown, Canoo, Virgin Orbit, Astra) — a filed, dated, checkable legal disclosure, not sentiment; this is the highest-confidence signal in the entire brief because it is a bright-line fact, not an inference.

signals.name: Runway compression rate (hard gate)
signals.weight_or_role: Disqualifying gate — fires when cash/quarterly-burn quarters-of-runway is both low (<2 quarters) and compressing quarter over quarter
signals.computation: cash_and_short_term_investments / trailing-quarter operating burn, computed each 10-Q/10-K, tracked as a time series per name; flag when the ratio both drops below 2 and its rate of decline accelerates (Virgin Orbit pattern: ~5 quarters -> under 2 in one filing)
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts API (cash, opex, OCF tags) — free, ~1-minute processing delay after filing acceptance
signals.why: Named explicitly in the graveyard discriminators as mattering more than the absolute cash figure; the empirical study's own runway_years feature is a weak coin-flip (AUC 0.48-0.53) as a STATIC number, but the graveyard cases show the RATE of compression, not the level, is what leads bankruptcy by 4-5 months — this system computes the derivative, not the level.

signals.name: Governance concentration / related-party self-dealing (hard gate)
signals.weight_or_role: Disqualifying gate
signals.computation: DEF 14A + 10-K related-party-transactions footnote scan for (a) board chairman/largest shareholder installing self as CEO, (b) payments to CEO-affiliated private entities at large multiples of revenue
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search + DEF 14A filings (free)
signals.why: Verified graveyard case (Canoo/Aquila) where this exact structure preceded confirmed self-dealing found later in the same company's own 10-K; removes the independent check that would normally catch fabricated order books.

signals.name: Exchange-compliance / delinquent-filing notices (hard gate)
signals.weight_or_role: Disqualifying gate
signals.computation: Scan for Item 3.01 8-Ks (NYSE/Nasdaq minimum-bid or filing-deficiency notices) and NT 10-K/NT 20-F delinquent-filing notices
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search / submissions API (free, filed within days of the triggering event)
signals.why: Named as a dated, cheap, pre-narrative tripwire in the graveyard discriminators (Arrival's NT 10-K preceded its collapse by months) — administrative fact, not opinion.

signals.name: Executive/CFO departure tied to a disclosed funding gap or audit-committee investigation
signals.weight_or_role: Disqualifying gate
signals.computation: Parse Item 5.02 8-K departure language for explicit funding-gap or investigation framing, versus generic 'personal reasons' boilerplate
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search + submissions API (free, 8-K due within 4 business days)
signals.why: Explicitly flagged in the graveyard discriminators as a much stronger signal than a bare departure fact when the filing language itself names the cause (Lordstown, Velodyne, Luminar).

signals.name: Binding-demand verification of any anchor-customer/contract announcement
signals.weight_or_role: Conditional promoter — an announced contract only becomes a positive supporting flag after this check passes; otherwise it is discarded, never scored positive
signals.computation: Cross-reference an 8-K/press-release 'order'/'LOI'/'design win' against the risk-factor language for deposit/no-easy-termination-clause AND against subsequent 10-Qs for delivered units or recognized revenue growth
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search + XBRL revenue tags across the following 2-4 quarters (free)
signals.why: The graveyard discriminators are explicit that the raw announcement is indistinguishable between RIDE/GOEV (hollow) and AMD/CRWV (real, cash-backed) — the binding+confirmed-in-arrears check is what the data itself says actually separates them; this is not itself a scriptable numeric field end-to-end (requires reading exhibit text), so it is only partially automatable.

signals.name: Dilution / share-count growth (shares_growth_yoy)
signals.weight_or_role: Low-moderate weight supporting signal — the single strongest AUC in the empirical study, but capped weight because the study itself says it needs quality decomposition
signals.computation: YoY growth in diluted shares outstanding (10-K/10-Q cover page + XBRL), ideally decomposed by counterparty (strategic/informed money vs. high-cost distress paper) via 8-K Item 1.01/424B5 text where feasible
signals.data_source: TradingView scanner API (free, keyless) for the raw ratio; SEC EDGAR 8-K/424B5 text for the quality decomposition
signals.why: Verified in today's empirical study: AUC 0.61 (all, n=202/227), 0.59 (tech_small, n=51/79) — the highest AUC of any tested feature, directionally consistent with every case-study winner (ENPH/TSLA/NBIS/APLD/CRWV all diluted materially pre-inflection) — but the same study and the graveyard notes both warn the identical raw fact (dilutive financing) also marks failed names (RGTI's 11% venture debt, APLD's 9% preferred, QBTS's IP-pledged loan), so weight stays capped rather than dominant.

signals.name: Distressed-but-funded ensemble (gross_margin, ocf_ttm, mom_6m/12m, drawdown_3y)
signals.weight_or_role: Low weight, used only as a combined ensemble tag ('distressed-but-funded profile'), never scored individually
signals.computation: Combine the four features, each already below-0.5 AUC individually in the empirical study, into a single categorical flag when a name is simultaneously low-margin, cash-burning, low-momentum, and deeply drawn-down relative to matched controls
signals.data_source: TradingView scanner API (free, keyless, quarterly/TTM fields)
signals.why: AUC 0.41/0.41/0.39/0.39/0.33 (all-sample) — individually below coin-flip in the direction of 'winners look WORSE', meaning the correct scoring direction is inverted from naive intuition; kept only as a low-weight ensemble context tag per the study's own framing that winners in this cohort look distressed, not because any one feature is independently strong.

signals.name: 13D activist-stake filing / sudden 13F filer-count jump
signals.weight_or_role: Low weight, confirming-only supporting flag
signals.computation: Monitor Schedule 13D filings (5%+ stake, board-seat intent) and quarter-over-quarter 13F filer-count for the name
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search / structured 13F datasets (free; 13D within 10 days of crossing threshold, 13F up to 45-day lag)
signals.why: Only one clean, genuinely leading case in the entire brief (APLD/Oasis 13D, 13 months lead); three of four case instances were coincident with or lagging the run, and no empirical AUC test exists for this family at all — kept as context, not a primary driver.

signals.name: Bare insider Form-4 buy/sell direction — explicitly EXCLUDED as a standalone signal
signals.weight_or_role: Excluded / zero weight (documented refutation-in-practice)
signals.computation: N/A — deliberately not scored
signals.data_source: N/A
signals.why: In 5+ of the brief's own winner instances (PLTR, SMCI, APLD, QBTS, RKLB) insider selling or zero open-market buying preceded or accompanied the run, including one confirmed false positive (VRT's 13-Form-4 cluster was $0.00 compensation vesting, not conviction buying) — the naive direction read is wrong or null often enough within winners alone that it fails the evidence-first bar and is excluded rather than down-weighted.

signals.name: Narrative/attention (EDGAR first-mention scan, analyst-rating divergence)
signals.weight_or_role: Triage-only lead-generation trigger — decides which names get a deeper filing check; explicitly ZERO scoring weight
signals.computation: Keyword first-mention scan (10-K/10-Q/8-K) for sector-specific reframing language; analyst-rating-vs-price divergence tracking
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search (free); free-tier analyst-rating aggregators
signals.why: The graveyard discriminators show narrative/attention build-up (celebrity CEOs, 'AI'/'autonomous' framing) was AT LEAST as strong in NKLA/RIDE/GOEV/Arrival as in any winner — a textbook look-alike that cannot discriminate alone, so it is used only to decide where to spend the deeper, more expensive binding-demand/governance checks.

proposals.thesis: There is currently no validated 'core' signal family in this brief's own evidence — the empirical AUC study shows standard fundamentals are near-coin-flip (0.48-0.55) in the exact pre-profit tech-small-cap population targeted, and every qualitative case-study family (anchor-customer, capex, insider/institutional, narrative, financing, price/flow, supply-chain, policy, hiring/patents) is explicitly graded 'supporting, not core' with a named survivorship confound. The one category of evidence with real, verified case-level separating power in this dossier is the graveyard discriminators — going-concern language, hollow-vs-binding order books, governance self-dealing, runway compression, exchange-compliance notices, funding-gap-tied departures — all of which are DISQUALIFIERS (they identify failure, not success). So Bumper Radar's honest design is a disqualification-first screener: it does not claim to find the next sector leader; it filters OUT the graveyard-pattern names from the emerging-sector small-cap universe, ranks survivors by the one empirically-nontrivial supporting feature (dilution quality), and reports a wide, mostly-abstaining probability band rather than a confident pick — with every claim traceable to a filing and a judge agent that explains and flags but never overrides the deterministic score.
proposals.universe_definition: US-listed (EDGAR-filing) common equity, market cap $50M-$3B (below $50M excluded for data/liquidity reliability; above $3B excluded as already too large to be a pre-rerating 'bumper' candidate), in one of three sectors: quantum computing, physical AI/robotics, AI infrastructure (compute/power/datacenter supply chain) — classified by SIC code plus the repo's existing curated capital-web graph, not by self-description. Must be pre-profit: trailing-twelve-month net income < 0 per XBRL NetIncomeLoss. Must have at least 2 quarters of filing history as a public company (excludes brand-new S-1 filers with no track record to gate-check) and at least one quarter since any SPAC-merger close (excludes pre-merger SPAC shells, which are a distinct instrument-risk category per the base-rate evidence). Excludes: OTC/pink-sheet-only listings, ADRs/foreign private issuers filing 20-F/6-F with materially thinner XBRL coverage (flagged, scored with wider abstention rather than excluded outright, since ASTS/IONQ-adjacent names may file 20-F), and any name already profitable on a TTM basis (moves it out of the 'pre-rerating' thesis entirely). Point-in-time discipline for backtesting: universe membership at any historical date T is reconstructed using only filings accepted on or before T — never today's SIC classification or today's known profitability applied retroactively.

backtest_protocol: Freeze-then-test, per references/edge-detection-method.md §0/§2: define the edge-detector's rules (capital-web edge-gain trigger, gate thresholds, certainty ladder) on a TRAIN slice, persist the parameters (JSON, git-tracked), and never refit against TEST-window dates. A version that refits per-run has already broken the protocol.

Historical universe, reconstructed point-in-time (this is the hard part, because scripts/aiinvest/capital_web.py's EDGES list and quantum_capital_web.py/physical_ai_capital_web.py are curated WITH HINDSIGHT as of 2026-05 -- using them as-is to backtest is look-ahead by construction). Build three cohorts from the brief's own case lists, each ticker time-stamped to its OWN filing history via scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py + xbrl.py: (a) winners (NVDA/VRT/PLTR/CRWV/NBIS/IREN/APLD/RKLB/ASTS/QBTS/OKLO/ENPH/SMCI/TSLA/SOUN), (b) graveyard failures (NKLA/RIDE/GOEV/Lordstown/Canoo/Arrival/Hyliion/MicroVision/BigBear.ai/Velodyne/Luminar/Virgin Orbit/Astra/Virgin Galactic/Momentus), (c) a neutral sample of pre-profit small caps in the same three sectors that neither ran nor collapsed -- omitting (c) selects on outcome and is the single most common way this kind of study fools itself.

For every ticker, re-derive what the detector would have flagged using ONLY filings/news dated before each candidate 'edge' event -- re-run edgar.py full-text search and news_graph.detect_candidate_edges against the as-filed EDGAR timestamp, not against today's capital_web.py graph. Any signal computed from a 2026-vintage curated edge list applied to a pre-2026 event is leakage; quarantine and exclude it rather than quietly patching.

Gate 1 -- Separation: bootstrap the conditional-mean difference (P(re-rate within horizon) | edge-flag vs no-flag) with BH-FDR correction across every signal family tested this session (economic-link, runway, dilution, going-concern, order-binding, momentum/drawdown, R&D), not just the ones that look good -- the brief's own empirical study already shows most financial-statement AUCs near 0.5, so expect most families to fail this gate and say so.

Gate 2 -- Fast detection: for each flagged episode, measure the lag between the edge's FILING date (8-K/10-K/full-text-search hit) and the date the retrospective label (>2x re-rate) would have been assigned; require lag < 12 months (the horizon this system claims to lead by). The brief already flags NVDA's Ex-99.1 and VRT's 10-K as sometimes-coincident (0-8mo) rather than leading -- don't let those episodes count as passes.

Gate 3 -- Edge survival: rho = online_edge (using only causally-available data at flag time) / retrospective_edge (using the full-hindsight capital-web graph) >= 0.7. Given the graph is manually curated and stale-by-construction (as_of 2026-05), expect rho to be materially below 1 -- report the actual ratio, don't round up.

Count independent EVENTS, not rows or dates: the unit is one company's one edge-gain episode (e.g. 'NBIS-Nvidia relationship disclosed'), not each daily price row or each 8-K in a cluster of related filings about the same deal. With ~15 winners + ~15 failures + a neutral sample, expect on the order of 20-40 independent episodes total -- small-n; report exact count and use sign-test/Wilcoxon on episode-level outcomes, per edge-detection-method.md §4, not a day-weighted t-test.

Era-test: split by filing-date era (pre-2023 vs 2023-2025 vs 2026, given the AI/quantum/robotics narrative itself is era-specific and crowded post-2023) -- train the detector's thresholds on one era, score the next. A detector that only works in the exact 2023-2025 AI-capex window it was built on is regime-fitted, not structural.

Benchmark: compare the flagged cohort's forward return distribution to a sector ETF/analog (e.g. an equal-weight basket of the same-sector neutral sample) rather than to zero -- the point of this system is ranking precision (does the top of the flagged list outperform the sector median), not absolute return forecasting, and that should be stated as the actual benchmark rather than 'beats the market'.

Costs/cash/tax/wrapper come last and are secondary here since this is a screening/detection system, not a trading rule -- skip position-level P&L modeling entirely per CLAUDE.md's IBKR account-data prohibition (no account data is used anywhere in this design) and instead report only detection precision/recall and lead-time distributions.

Adversarial review stage (superpowers:systematic-debugging / verification-before-completion, sub-agent on model:'sonnet' per CLAUDE.md §1 rule 7): a separate agent whose brief is to find look-ahead paths in the capital-web-edge reconstruction and undercount independent events, and to demand the exact number of signal variants tried (denominator for every claim) before any gate result is trusted.
build_plan_first_two_weeks: Day 1: superpowers:brainstorming session (CLAUDE.md rule 1) to lock the exact edge-gain trigger definition and the three-cohort backtest universe before writing code; output a one-page spec, not code.

Days 1-3: extend scripts/aiinvest/capital_web.py (and physical_ai_capital_web.py / quantum_capital_web.py) with a snapshot/diff function -- persist a timestamped JSON per run under data/capital_web_history/ (or data/private/ if it would ever touch account-linked names, which it should not here) and add edge_diff(old, new) -> new/changed edges. TDD per scripts/tests/test_capital_web.py pattern.

Days 2-4: extend scripts/aiinvest/news_graph.py's existing detect_candidate_edges / classify_certainty pipeline into a persistent review queue (new module scripts/aiinvest/edge_queue.py) that stores candidate edges with certainty (filed/reported/rumored), source URL, and promotion status -- reuse the existing certainty classifier rather than rewriting it.

Days 3-6: new module scripts/aiinvest/gates.py implementing the graveyard-discriminator gates as pure functions consuming already-pulled data: runway_months() from xbrl.py cash/burn facts, dilution shares_growth_yoy() from tradingview.py/xbrl.py, going_concern_flag() via edgar.py full-text search for 'going concern'/'substantial doubt', and order_binding_score() as a manual-review-required flag (EDGAR full-text hit + human confirmation, since the brief is explicit this cannot be fully automated). TDD each function against scripts/tests/test_gates.py with known winner/graveyard filings as fixtures.

Days 5-7: universe filter wired into scripts/aiinvest/screener.py -- market cap band, sector tag (quantum/physical-AI/AI-infra via existing quantum_stack.py/physical_ai_stack.py/ai_stack.py layer taxonomy), pre-profit flag (negative ocf_ttm), and exclusion rules (already-re-rated names, non-EDGAR filers, shell/no-capex names).

Days 8-9: new module scripts/aiinvest/bumper_judge.py -- assembles the judge agent's input bundle (edge diff + certainty, gate results, context signals) and dispatches to a sub-agent on model:'sonnet' per CLAUDE.md rule 7 for the rubric-based adjudication; the orchestrator (this session's model) never runs the judge itself.

Days 9-11: point-in-time backtest fixture -- hand-build the winners/graveyard/neutral ticker list with filing-date-stamped edge/gate values (not today's curated graph) in scripts/tests/fixtures/bumper_backtest_universe.json; this is the single highest-risk, most time-consuming step and should not be shortcut.

Days 11-13: backtest harness (extend scripts/aiinvest/backtest.py or add scripts/bumper_backtest.py) implementing the three gates, BH-FDR bootstrap, and episode-level (not row-level) event counting from edge-detection-method.md.

Day 14: adversarial review pass (superpowers:systematic-debugging, sonnet sub-agent, high reasoning effort per CLAUDE.md rule 7) on the backtest for look-ahead leakage and event-undercounting before any gate result is reported as passing; write up findings, do not fix-and-declare-done in the same pass.
proposals.expected_base_rate_and_payoff: Per the supplied brief's directly-opened base rates (Ritter's IPO dataset and the deSPAC studies), the unconditional prior for this exact population -- unprofitable, small-sales issuers -- is unfavorable on average: median 3-year buy-and-hold for unprofitable IPOs is roughly -25% to -31% market-adjusted, and only ~1.7-7.7% of the broader IPO population ever exceeds +200-500% over 3 years. The tech-specific unprofitable-small-sales subset does better on a MEAN basis (+28.4% raw, still -19.2% market-adjusted) but that mean is carried by a small right tail, not the median case. Today's empirical study (n~30-230/arm depending on subgroup) reinforces this: financial-statement features barely separate eventual winners from matched controls in the tech_small population (AUC 0.48-0.59 for growth/R&D/runway; the only feature clearing 0.55 anywhere is shares_growth_yoy at 0.61, i.e. dilution-funded runway, not fundamentals). Given this, the system's realistic job is NOT to assign a high absolute probability of success to any single name -- base rates argue against that -- but to improve RANKING precision within an already-narrow universe: surface the minority of names carrying a real, filed (not rumored) economic-link edge AND passing the graveyard's binding/runway/governance gates, from the majority that will not re-rate. Expected payoff shape is strongly right-skewed/fat-tailed (a small number of large winners, most flagged names flat-to-down or delisted), so the judge's calibrated probability bands should default LOW (e.g. single-digit to ~15% base case for "becomes a sector-leader re-rate candidate within 12 months") and only move up meaningfully when multiple independent, filed (not reported/rumored) gates pass simultaneously -- and even then, per McLean & Pontiff, any historical edge size should be discounted for publication/crowding decay since this exact playbook (economic-link screening) is not proprietary.

guardrails: Never phrase output as advice, a recommendation, or a buy/sell signal -- output is a research-flag probability band with reasons, explicitly labeled educational/research only, consistent with CLAUDE.md §0/§8 and this task's ground rules.

Cite-or-abstain: every one of the three reasons must name the exact filing/URL/endpoint and its retrieved_at date (per references/data-schema.md's source/source_class/retrieved_at stamp), or be explicitly labeled 'reported' or 'rumored' per news_graph.py's classify_certainty output. A reason with no citable source is dropped, not asserted.

Abstain on thin data: if XBRL coverage is missing (common -- the repo's own study notes ~45% coverage), if no capital-web/candidate edge exists at all, or if the only supporting edge is 'rumored' with no independent corroboration, output MUST be 'abstain -- insufficient data' rather than a forced probability.

Hard-gate the graveyard discriminators BEFORE any positive edge counts: an economic-link edge that fails the binding-vs-hollow check (no deposit, easy-out termination clause), or that coexists with a going-concern flag, a founder-as-chairman-installs-self-CEO governance structure, or a compressing runway, cannot produce a probability above the system's low-base-rate floor regardless of how prominent the named counterparty is -- this directly encodes the NKLA/RIDE/GOEV lesson that the raw announcement looks identical in busts.

Explicitly banned as a standalone input: bare insider Form-4 buy/sell direction (repeatedly wrong-signed in the brief's own winner case studies) and narrative/attention/press-coverage volume alone (present in both winners and graveyard names at equal intensity) -- these may appear only as context color inside a reason, never as the basis for a probability move.

Certainty ladder governs weight, not just labeling: filed > reported > rumored. A rumored-only edge caps the output at 'abstain' or the lowest probability band unless corroborated by an independent filed source within a defined window.
Judge runs as a sub-agent on model:'sonnet' at high reasoning effort (CLAUDE.md rule 7) -- the orchestrator dispatches it and reviews its output, never runs the judge itself on the top model.
No order-placing, no account-data inputs of any kind (CLAUDE.md §11 is out of scope here by design -- this system never touches brokerage MCP tools).

State the number of signal variants/thresholds tried when reporting any backtest result feeding the rubric's calibration, per edge-detection-method.md §8 -- an uncounted denominator invalidates the calibration claim.
inputs: Capital-web edge diff: new or changed edges between the last two capital_web.py/physical_ai_capital_web.py/quantum_capital_web.py snapshots for the candidate ticker (src/dst/type/attrs + as_of dates for both snapshots).

News-derived candidate edges: news_graph.py's detect_candidate_edges output for the ticker over the trailing window -- tagged entities, deal-language trigger matched, classify_certainty result (filed/reported/rumored), and source URL.

Filings gate results from scripts/aiinvest/gates.py (to be built): runway_months (cash ÷ trailing burn from xbrl.py), shares_growth_yoy (dilution trend), going_concern_flag (EDGAR full-text 'going concern'/'material weakness' hit), order_binding_score (manual-review flag on deposit/termination-clause language), and any exchange-compliance (Item 3.01) or executive-departure-tied-to-funding-gap (Item 5.02) flags.

Context signals: momentum/drawdown (mom_6m_pre, mom_12m_pre, drawdown_3y from tradingview.py), short-interest crowding (FINRA, when available), and sector/layer tag from ai_stack.py / quantum_stack.py / physical_ai_stack.py.
Provenance pack: every input's source, source_class, and retrieved_at stamp, so the judge can enforce the cite-or-abstain guardrail mechanically rather than by self-report.
judge_agent.outputs: A calibrated probability BAND (not a point estimate) for 'becomes a sector-visible re-rate candidate within 12 months' drawn from a small discrete set of bands (e.g. abstain / <5% / 5-15% / 15-30% / >30%, deliberately low-ceilinged given the base rates below), plus exactly three reasons ranked by contribution -- at minimum one must cite the economic-link edge (with certainty level), one must cite a filings gate (pass/fail with the specific number, e.g. 'runway 7.2mo per 10-Q liquidity footnote'), and one must be a context signal -- each reason carrying its source citation and retrieved_at date, or explicitly marked reported/rumored.
rubric: Step 1 (hard gate, per graveyard discriminators): does the candidate edge show binding terms (deposit, no easy termination) AND is there no going-concern/governance red flag? If either fails, cap the band at the floor regardless of edge prominence.
Step 2: classify the edge's certainty (filed/reported/rumored) using news_graph.py's classify_certainty; rumored-only with no filed corroboration forces 'abstain' or floor band.
Step 3: score the filings gates (runway, dilution trend, order-binding, compliance/departure flags) as pass/fail/unknown; 'unknown' on more than half the gates forces 'abstain'.

Step 4: layer context (momentum/drawdown/short-interest) only to adjust WITHIN a band already set by steps 1-3, never to move between bands on its own -- per the brief's own finding that these features are crowding/context, not discriminators.

Step 5: apply the base-rate ceiling from the backtest (see expected_base_rate_and_payoff) -- do not output a band above what the historical episode-level hit rate in the matching sector/era supports, and say which historical episode-cohort the ceiling was drawn from.
Step 6: write the three reasons, each with a citation; if any required reason cannot be sourced, downgrade to 'abstain' rather than publish an uncited reason.

proposals.name: Bumper Radar
risks: Survivorship / no failure-side edge data: the repo's capital-web graph (capital_web.py, physical_ai_capital_web.py, quantum_capital_web.py) only tracks CURRENT, mostly-successful public names as of 2026-05 -- it was never built with graveyard failures (NKLA, RIDE, GOEV, Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, Hyliion, MicroVision, BigBear.ai, Luminar, Virgin Orbit, Astra) as nodes, so there is no existing point-in-time record of what THEIR economic-link edges looked like pre-collapse. Building that comparison set from scratch is the single biggest, most error-prone piece of the two-week plan (see backtest_protocol) and if skipped, the whole system is validated only against known winners -- exactly the failure mode edge-detection-method.md warns about.

Look-ahead via the curated graph itself: capital_web.py's EDGES list is hand-curated with the benefit of hindsight (an as_of snapshot, not a live time series). Any backtest that scores historical episodes against TODAY's graph rather than a reconstructed as-filed-date graph will overstate detection performance -- this has to be actively guarded against, not just noted.

Certainty classification is heuristic: news_graph.py's classify_certainty and detect_candidate_edges rely on deal-language keyword triggers and word-boundary matching -- both false positives (a hedged/conditional press release read as 'filed') and false negatives (an EDGAR 8-K whose language doesn't match the trigger list) are likely at the margins, and neither has been measured for precision/recall in this repo yet.

Small independent-event count: per edge-detection-method.md §4, with roughly 15 winners + 15 graveyard names + a neutral sample, the honest number of independent episodes is likely in the 20-40 range -- underpowered for anything beyond directional, non-definitive conclusions; any p-value reported on this backtest should be read as suggestive, not confirmatory, and the write-up must say so plainly.

Coverage gaps limit scale: SEC XBRL coverage is ~45% per the empirical study already run; short interest is biweekly and lagged; 13F is 45-day-lagged; PatentsView/USAspending lags are inferred, not verified. The system will systematically have thinner data (more abstains) for exactly the newest, smallest, most 'bumper-like' names -- which is also where the abstain guardrail will fire most often, potentially making the system quietest exactly where a user most wants a signal.

Order-binding verification is not fully automatable: the graveyard's own discriminators say the highest-value check (deposit/termination-clause language) requires reading contract exhibits, not a keyword pull -- this gate will bottleneck on manual/LLM-assisted filing review, which is slower and noisier than the mechanical gates.

Playwright-sourced enrichment (e.g. GuruFocus valuation cross-check) must respect the Mode A/Mode B concurrency contract (CLAUDE.md §3) -- a careless Mode-A tab opened during a Mode-B gated GuruFocus pull would poison or reset the gate; this is a process risk for whoever operationalizes the judge's context-signal gathering, not a modeling risk.

Base-rate ceiling risk: because the target population's historical base rate for 'true bumper' outcomes is low (per expected_base_rate_and_payoff), any judge miscalibration tends toward FALSE POSITIVES (overconfident bands) rather than false negatives, since users searching for 'the next bumper' will be inclined to read a mid-band probability as more actionable than the base rate supports -- the abstain and floor-band guardrails exist specifically to counter this, and must not be relaxed under user pressure to 'give a number.'
