Regulatory/reputational: even with abstain-or-cite guardrails, a probability BAND output on a live, pre-profit small cap is easy to misread as investment guidance despite disclaimers -- this is the reason the rubric caps bands low and requires three sourced reasons rather than a single confident score, and any productization of this design should re-confirm that framing survives contact with an actual user interface.

signals.computation: Snapshot capital_web.py / physical_ai_capital_web.py / quantum_capital_web.py's EDGES on a schedule; diff consecutive snapshots for NEW edges (src=candidate small-cap, dst=a large/anchor counterparty, type in customer/compute/infra_partner/equity per the repo's edge-semantics memory) touching the candidate ticker.
signals.data_source: In-repo curated capital-web graph (scripts/aiinvest/capital_web.py etc.), free, no network call, refresh cadence = whenever a human promotes a candidate edge.
signals.name: capital_web_edge_gain
signals.weight_or_role: core / primary trigger -- this is the requested economic-links-first signal; a name with zero new edge cannot enter the flagged list at all.
signals.why: Per the task's angle: a small cap gaining a binding edge to a giant is the earliest-observable form of most of the brief's supporting families (anchor-customer, capex/capacity, supply-chain) without waiting for revenue to show up in financials, where the empirical study shows near-null separation (AUC 0.48-0.55 in tech_small).

signals.computation: Run news_graph.py's detect_candidate_edges over trailing news for the ticker; classify_certainty() tags each hit filed/reported/rumored based on the underlying source (8-K/press release vs news article vs unconfirmed chatter).
signals.data_source: Finnhub company-news API (free tier, keyed) + Yahoo Finance RSS (free, keyless) feeding scripts/aiinvest/news_graph.py.
signals.name: candidate_edge_certainty
signals.weight_or_role: core / gating multiplier on capital_web_edge_gain -- a rumored-only hit does not clear the judge's floor band.
signals.why: The brief's own case studies show 'order/LOI announced' looks identical across NKLA/RIDE/GOEV (hollow) and NVDA/CRWV (real) at announcement time; certainty classification plus the binding-check gate below is the graveyard's named fix, not the raw edge alone.

signals.computation: order_binding_score(): EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) for the underlying contract exhibit language + manual/LLM-assisted read for deposit and termination-clause terms; flag as binding / non-binding / unknown.
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search + filing exhibits, free, via scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py.
signals.name: gate_order_binding
signals.weight_or_role: gate (hard) -- non-binding or unknown caps the probability band at the floor regardless of edge prominence.
signals.why: Directly encodes the graveyard's top discriminator: 'treat every order/pre-order/LOI as worthless until confirmed' (deposit, no easy-out termination, delivered units in subsequent 10-Qs).

signals.computation: runway_months = latest disclosed cash & short-term investments (XBRL) / trailing-quarter operating burn (from the same filing's cash-flow statement), via xbrl.py.
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts API (data.sec.gov), free, no auth, near-real-time after filing acceptance.
signals.name: gate_runway
signals.weight_or_role: gate (hard) -- a specific disclosed runway under ~1 quarter (Canoo-style) caps the band; the empirical study's runway_years AUC is coin-flip (0.48-0.53) as a STANDALONE ranker, so this is used as a floor/ceiling gate, not a scoring feature.
signals.why: Graveyard discriminator: 'a SPECIFIC disclosed runway number... is a hard, dated, near-term warning' -- distinct from boilerplate going-concern language.

signals.computation: going_concern_flag: EDGAR full-text search for 'going concern' / 'substantial doubt' / material-weakness language in the trailing 10-K/10-Q.
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search, free, via edgar.py.
signals.name: gate_going_concern
signals.weight_or_role: gate (hard, but low-discrimination on its own) -- present caps the band; absent is necessary-but-not-sufficient, not a green light.
signals.why: Boilerplate going-concern language is 'nearly universal and low-signal' per the graveyard notes, but its ABSENCE combined with other passing gates is part of the necessary floor the same notes describe.

signals.computation: shares_growth_yoy (diluted shares outstanding, YoY %) from tradingview.py/xbrl.py.
signals.data_source: TradingView scanner API (free, keyless POST) or XBRL companyfacts, quarterly cadence.
signals.name: dilution_shares_growth_yoy
signals.weight_or_role: supporting -- highest AUC of any tested feature in the empirical study (0.61 all-sample, 0.59 tech_small); used as a context multiplier, not a gate.
signals.why: The study's strongest quantitative discriminator: winners diluted MORE than matched controls, consistent with equity-funded capacity build-out buying runway to the inflection -- but per the study itself this must be paired with the runway/burn gates above, not used alone.

signals.computation: mom_6m_pre, mom_12m_pre, drawdown_3y from tradingview.py price history.
signals.data_source: TradingView scanner API, free, keyless.
signals.name: momentum_and_drawdown_context
signals.weight_or_role: supporting/context only -- adjusts within a band already set by the gates, never moves bands alone.
signals.why: AUCs are all below 0.5 (0.33-0.39) meaning winners were MORE beaten-down/lower-momentum pre-run than controls -- informative as a 'hated, beaten-down, funded' profile check but explicitly not a standalone bullish/bearish timer per the brief's own price_and_flow analysis.

signals.computation: rnd_to_rev (R&D / revenue) from tradingview.py.
signals.data_source: TradingView scanner API, free, keyless, quarterly.
signals.name: rnd_intensity_context
signals.weight_or_role: supporting, low weight -- AUC 0.46-0.48 in tech/tech_small (below 0.5), so treated as color only.
signals.why: Included for completeness since it's cheap and free, but the empirical study shows winners were if anything LESS R&D-intensive than matched controls in this population -- explicitly not weighted as a discriminator.

signals.computation: N/A -- deliberately excluded as an input.
signals.data_source: N/A
signals.name: insider_form4_direction (EXCLUDED)
signals.weight_or_role: refuted for this use -- explicitly banned from the judge's inputs.
signals.why: Repeatedly wrong-signed or null in the brief's own winner case studies (PLTR, SMCI, APLD, QBTS, RKLB all show selling or zero buying pre-run; a VRT Form-4 cluster that looked like conviction was $0 comp-vesting). Listed here only to document that it was considered and rejected, per the epistemic-honesty rule against silently omitting a tested family.

proposals.thesis: Economic-links, not financial statements, are the earliest observable evidence that a pre-profit small cap in an emerging sector is being drawn into a giant's value chain -- and the repo's own empirical study run today confirms why this matters: revenue growth/acceleration and R&D intensity are near-coin-flip discriminators (AUC 0.48-0.55) in the exact tech_small population this system targets, while the strongest quantitative signal available (shares_growth_yoy, AUC 0.61) is a financing/dilution proxy, not a fundamentals one. The system therefore treats a new, binding, filed capital-web edge (customer/compute/infra_partner/equity link to a named large counterparty) as the PRIMARY trigger, and uses filings-based gates lifted directly from the graveyard discriminators (binding-vs-hollow order language, disclosed runway math, going-concern/governance flags) to suppress the exact false-positive pattern that made NKLA/RIDE/GOEV indistinguishable from NVDA/CRWV at announcement time. A judge agent adjudicates certainty (filed/reported/rumored) and outputs a deliberately low-ceilinged probability band with sourced reasons, not a forecast -- because the base rates for this population (below) argue strongly against high-confidence point predictions.
proposals.universe_definition: US-listed (SEC EDGAR filer; ADRs with 20-F/6-K included, OTC/pink-sheet excluded for filing-cadence reliability) equities tagged to one of the repo's three tracked emerging-sector taxonomies: quantum (quantum_stack.py layer tags), physical AI/robotics (physical_ai_stack.py), and AI infrastructure (ai_stack.py L1-chips/L2-infra/neocloud layers) -- explicitly excluding the already-recognized mega-cap leaders those modules also track (NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL-class names), since the system's job is catching names BEFORE they join that tier, not scoring the tier itself. Market-cap band: roughly $50M-$3B (below $50M: filing/liquidity too thin for reliable XBRL coverage per the study's ~45% coverage note; above $3B: no longer a 'small cap' in the sense the brief's case studies use). Profitability filter: pre-profit by trailing OCF (ocf_ttm < 0) or trailing net income < 0 -- this is the exact population the empirical study was run on. Exclusions: (1) names already up >3x from their prior-12-month low (the re-rate the system exists to anticipate has already happened -- scoring these is hindsight, not detection); (2) financial/investment shells with no disclosed operating revenue AND no disclosed capex (SPAC pre-merger shells); (3) names with no SEC filing in the trailing 12 months (delisted/dormant -- these belong in the graveyard backtest cohort, not the live-screening universe); (4) any name whose only available data is brokerage-account-derived (not applicable here since this system uses no IBKR/account inputs at all, consistent with CLAUDE.md §11 -- flagging explicitly that this design never needs that exception).

proposals.name: Bumper Radar: Judge-Panel Screen for Pre-Profit Sector-Leader Candidates
proposals.thesis: A quantitative screen alone cannot pick tomorrow's sector leader in quantum/physical-AI/AI-infrastructure: today's empirical study shows the standard fundamental features barely separate historical winners from matched pre-profit controls (AUC 0.51-0.61 for growth/dilution, and BELOW 0.5 for margin/cash-flow/momentum/drawdown — winners look MORE distressed, not less). Meanwhile the graveyard record shows the qualitative "story" signals (anchor customer, capacity buildout, narrative reframe) are present in equal measure in companies that went to zero — the same press release describes NVDA's cloud deals and Nikola's GM tie-up. Neither a pure quant screen nor pure narrative-matching discriminates. What the graveyard data says DOES discriminate is reading primary filings for a small set of checkable facts a numeric field cannot capture: is the demand binding (deposit, no easy termination clause, delivered units in the next 10-Q) or hollow; is dilution funding a real buildout or masking a going-concern; do insiders own the story or are they exiting into it; does delivered substance lag the narrative; is a policy/technology catalyst genuinely dated and leading or coincident hype. That is a job for judgment applied to text, not a formula — hence a panel of narrow LLM judges, each scored against a graveyard-derived rubric with mandatory filing citations, whose combined and calibrated verdict — gated by a devil's-advocate that must argue the bear case — is the actual discriminator. The quant screen's only job is to keep the panel's expensive filing-reading work to a shortlist size; it is never itself the verdict.
proposals.universe_definition: US-exchange-listed (NYSE/NASDAQ, ADRs excluded for this v1 since EDGAR/XBRL coverage and Form 4/13D timeliness are the backbone of every judge) common equities in three sectors already modeled in this repo's capital-web pipelines: quantum computing (scripts/aiinvest/quantum_stack.py universe), physical AI/robotics (scripts/aiinvest/physical_ai_stack.py universe), and AI infrastructure/neocloud (scripts/aiinvest/ai_stack.py layers L1-chips through L3-infra/neocloud, excluding L5-application incumbents that are already profitable). Caps: market cap $50M-$5B (below $50M is de facto unlisted/illiquid and filing quality collapses; above $5B is no longer the 'months-before-re-rating' case this system targets — it is already a covered mega-cap). Pre-profit gate: trailing-twelve-month net income <0 OR trailing operating cash flow <0 (both computed from SEC XBRL companyfacts, matching study.py's existing feature pull). Exclusions: (1) pre-merger SPACs / SPACs still in trust (no operating filings to judge — re-admit only after de-SPAC close); (2) names with <2 quarters of post-listing 10-Q/10-K history (nothing for the judges to read); (3) OTC/pink-sheet and non-reporting foreign private issuers (no XBRL, no Form 4/13D timeliness); (4) names already flagged delinquent (NT 10-K/NT 20-F outstanding) — these get auto-routed to the graveyard-discriminator watch, not the bumper-candidate queue, per the repo's own discriminator list; (5) names with zero EDGAR full-text-search hits for the sector in the trailing 12 months (nothing to shortlist on). Universe refresh: quarterly full rebuild via the TradingView scanner REST endpoint (sector/industry columns, per providers/README.md) plus a weekly incremental sweep of new 8-Ks/S-1s in the three sectors to catch new listings between rebuilds.

signals.name: revenue_growth_yoy / revenue_acceleration
signals.weight_or_role: screen-only, low weight (near-null in target population)
signals.computation: YoY revenue growth and its second derivative from trailing 4 quarters of XBRL Revenues/RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts API (data.sec.gov) via scripts/aiinvest/xbrl.py; cross-check via TradingView scanner revenue_ttm columns
signals.why: Empirical study AUC 0.51 (all) / 0.48 (tech_small) for acceleration — a coin flip or worse in exactly this population; kept only as a cheap universe-narrowing filter (require the datum exist), never scored as a discriminator.

signals.name: shares_growth_yoy (dilution rate)
signals.weight_or_role: screen input, highest-weight quant feature (AUC 0.61)
signals.computation: YoY growth in weighted-average diluted shares outstanding from XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, cross-checked against 10-K/10-Q cover-page share counts
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts API via scripts/aiinvest/xbrl.py
signals.why: The single strongest AUC in the whole battery (0.61 all-sample, 0.59 tech_small) — winners dilute MORE than controls, consistent with equity-funded buildout. Used to prioritize the shortlist toward 'funded to build,' not to screen dilution OUT.

signals.name: cash-runway / burn-rate trend
signals.weight_or_role: screen input + feeds Dilution & Runway judge directly
signals.computation: cash+short-term investments / trailing-quarter operating cash burn, and the QoQ trend in that ratio (compression, not just level, per graveyard discriminator on Virgin Orbit)
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts (cash_n_short_term_invest, ocf) via scripts/aiinvest/xbrl.py
signals.why: Empirical AUC only 0.48-0.53 (near coin-flip) as a static feature, so it is demoted from a quant score to a compulsory input the Dilution & Runway judge must read qualitatively (financing subtype: strategic equity vs. covenant-heavy distress debt), per the brief's own finding that runway/financing quality, not the raw fact of raising capital, is what the graveyard cases separate on.

signals.name: R&D intensity (rnd_to_rev)
signals.weight_or_role: screen input, near-zero weight
signals.computation: trailing R&D expense / trailing revenue from XBRL ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense
signals.data_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts via scripts/aiinvest/xbrl.py
signals.why: AUC 0.46 (tech) / 0.48 (tech_small) — BELOW 0.5, meaning winners were if anything LESS R&D-intensive than controls in this population. Kept in the feature vector for completeness and as an input to the Narrative-vs-Delivery judge (is claimed innovation matched by spend), not as a scoring weight.

signals.name: momentum & drawdown (mom_6m/12m_pre, drawdown_3y)
signals.weight_or_role: screen input, inverted sense (context flag)
signals.computation: trailing 6/12-month price momentum and 3-year max drawdown at run-start-minus-3mo from Yahoo/TradingView monthly closes
signals.data_source: Yahoo Finance chart REST endpoint / TradingView scanner (scripts/aiinvest/yahoo.py, tradingview.py)
signals.why: All AUCs well below 0.5 (0.33-0.44) — winners were MORE beaten-down and lower-momentum than controls pre-run. Used as a context flag ('hated/crowded name near a cycle low') that raises a name's shortlist priority rather than lowering it, and feeds the Sector Timing judge.

signals.name: anchor-customer / contract disclosure (raw flag, unverified)
signals.weight_or_role: shortlist trigger only, never scored numerically
signals.computation: EDGAR full-text-search keyword hits ('customer concentration', named hyperscaler/OEM, contract/backlog language) in 8-K/10-K risk factors within trailing 12 months
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search API (efts.sec.gov) — no existing repo module; extends scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py
signals.why: Untested empirically (no AUC exists) and explicitly contaminated by graveyard look-alikes (RIDE, GOEV) at the announcement level. Used only to flag a name into the shortlist for the Contract Reality judge to verify bindingness — never a go/no-go by itself.

signals.name: capex / capacity disclosure (raw flag)
signals.weight_or_role: shortlist trigger only
signals.computation: EDGAR full-text-search hits for capacity/plant/fleet buildout language (Item 2 Properties, MD&A capex tables) plus XBRL PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment growth
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search + XBRL companyfacts via scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py / xbrl.py
signals.why: Identical fact pattern (capacity buildout ahead of revenue) describes both SMCI/NBIS-style winners and Lordstown/Canoo-style failures per the brief. Trigger for shortlisting + an input the Dilution & Runway and Contract Reality judges must reconcile against demand bindingness, not a standalone score.

signals.name: Form 4 insider transaction direction
signals.weight_or_role: explicitly NOT used as a bullish/bearish quant signal — judge input only
signals.computation: parse Form 4 transaction codes/shares/price per CIK over trailing 12 months (buy vs. sell vs. compensation-vesting at $0)
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text/submissions search filtered to form=='4' (data.sec.gov) — new parser module needed, reusing scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py's fetch_submissions
signals.why: The brief shows this sub-signal repeatedly wrong-signed within the winner set itself (Thiel/Karp selling into PLTR's run, a VRT Form-4 cluster that was $0 comp vesting mistaken for conviction buying). Explicitly downweighted to zero in the quant score; the Insider Conviction judge reads the actual transaction context (price, vesting vs. open-market, % of holdings) instead of trusting the sign.

signals.name: 13D activist stake / 13F filer-count jump
signals.weight_or_role: judge input, confirming not leading in most cases
signals.computation: detect new Schedule 13D filings (>5% stake, board-seat language) and quarter-over-quarter growth in distinct 13F filer count per CIK
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search / structured 13F datasets (data.sec.gov) — 45-day lag on 13F, near-real-time on 13D
signals.why: Only one clean leading example exists in the brief (APLD/Oasis 13D, 13 months lead); most instances are coincident with the catalyst itself. Feeds the Insider Conviction judge as one input among several, with the 45-day 13F lag explicitly flagged as stale for a fast-moving small cap.

signals.name: going-concern / material-weakness / delinquent-filing language
signals.weight_or_role: hard override — routes to auto-reject queue, bypasses judges
signals.computation: EDGAR full-text search for 'going concern', 'substantial doubt', Item 4.02 non-reliance 8-Ks, or an outstanding NT 10-K/NT 20-F for the CIK
signals.data_source: SEC EDGAR full-text search API
signals.why: The single most consistent, bright-line graveyard discriminator across every collapsed-name case study in the brief (Lordstown, Canoo, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Momentus). A hit here does not lower a score — it removes the name from the bumper-candidate queue entirely and routes it to a separate distress-watch list, since the brief's evidence treats this as near-deterministic of eventual failure, not merely correlated.

judge_agent.name: Judge Panel (5 narrow judges + calibrated aggregator + mandatory devil's-advocate)
inputs: The shortlisted ticker + CIK + sector layer (from the quant screen, capped at ~20-50 names/quarter for cost control)

All 8-K, 10-K, 10-Q, S-1/424B, and DEF 14A filings for the trailing 12-24 months, fetched via SEC EDGAR (scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py) and full-text search, restricted to filings dated on or before the frozen as-of date
XBRL structured facts (revenue, R&D, cash, shares outstanding, PP&E) from companyfacts, already computed by the quant screen (scripts/bumper/features.py)
Form 4 transaction history (raw, unfiltered by direction) and any 13D/13F filings for the CIK
The raw contract/capacity/going-concern EDGAR full-text-search hits (unverified flags) from the screen
The graveyard_discriminators list itself, embedded in each judge's system prompt as the rubric's source-of-truth (not a general 'use judgment' instruction)
rubric: Contract Reality judge — score 0-100 on: is there a named counterparty; is the deal backed by a deposit or non-cancellable term (vs. a bare LOI/pre-order); do subsequent 10-Qs show delivered units, recognized revenue, or growing RPO/backlog consistent with the announcement. Anything scoring on the announcement's existence alone, without a citation to a SUBSEQUENT filing confirming delivery, is capped at 40/100 regardless of how impressive the initial press release reads.

Dilution & Runway judge — score 0-100 on: financing counterparty quality (strategic/informed money at or near market vs. covenant-heavy distress paper — venture debt, high-coupon preferred, IP-pledged loans); whether disclosed runway is compressing or stable quarter-over-quarter; whether liquidity is conditioned on continued access to an ATM/shelf the company may not be able to use. A going-concern flag or NT-filing (from the screen's hard override) auto-fails this judge at 0/100.

Insider Conviction judge — score 0-100 on: net open-market buying vs. selling by direction AND magnitude as a % of holdings (not raw Form-4 count); explicit exclusion of $0-price compensation-vesting transactions from being counted as 'buying'; presence of a genuine 13D activist stake with a dated board-seat ask scores materially higher than a 13F filer-count uptick that coincides with the catalyst itself (coincident, not leading, per the brief).

Narrative-vs-Delivery judge — score 0-100 on: does the company's own operational disclosure (units shipped, capacity utilized, milestones hit on the schedule management itself set) keep pace with its narrative claims (earnings-call reframes, analyst-target narrative, EDGAR full-text-search keyword adoption); explicit penalty for management moving the goalposts (redefining a milestone, discontinuing the product line the backlog was built on, as in Astra) after missing it.

Sector Timing judge — score 0-100 on: is the catalyst a dated, agency-level, or filing-disclosed event with real lead time (e.g., an FCC/NRC rulemaking, a technical milestone independently verifiable via a third party like FERC/ERCOT), versus a macro/cohort-wide catalyst (ChatGPT-moment-style) that doesn't by itself pick this specific name; cross-checks the beaten-down-momentum/high-short-interest context flag against whether an actual catalyst has appeared to resolve it, since crowding alone (per the brief) is not a discriminator.
judge_agent.outputs: A calibrated probability BAND (not a point estimate — e.g. '8-18% probability of becoming a recognized sector leader within 24 months', derived from isotonic/logistic calibration of the blended judge score against the backtest's historical event outcomes, never presented as a precise number given the small-n calibration set); the TOP THREE reasons for the band, each with an inline filing citation (EDGAR accession number + URL + filing date); an explicit ABSTAIN flag when any judge cannot find enough filing coverage to score its rubric (e.g., <2 quarters of history, no Form 4 history at all); and the single strongest counter-argument surfaced by the devil's-advocate, printed even when the panel proceeds to a verdict.
guardrails: Never phrase output as advice, a recommendation, a buy/sell signal, or a price target — output is a research probability estimate for an educational research context only, and every response ends with that disclaimer.

Cite or abstain: every factual claim in a judge's rationale must carry a dereferenced EDGAR/FINRA/USAspending citation (URL + accession/date) that a verification step actually fetches and confirms contains the claimed language before the claim is kept; unverifiable claims are dropped, not softened.

Abstain on thin data: if fewer than 2 quarters of 10-Q/10-K history, no XBRL coverage, or a judge's required filing type is entirely absent, that judge must output ABSTAIN rather than force a score, and the aggregator must not silently impute a neutral value for an abstained judge — it flags the whole verdict LOW-CONFIDENCE and reports which judge abstained and why.

Mandatory devil's-advocate gate: a separate sub-agent instance, given the same filings, is briefed only to build the bear case using the graveyard_discriminators list, and must be run BEFORE the aggregator finalizes a verdict; if it surfaces an unaddressed hard-override condition (going concern, delinquent filing, hollow-order pattern with no delivery confirmation), the verdict is forced to ABSTAIN/REJECT regardless of the other four judges' scores.
Never launder rumor into fact: any deal, valuation, or catalyst not yet confirmed in a filed document is labeled reported/rumored explicitly in the output, never stated as settled.

Hard-coded exclusion of the brokerage/IBKR account tools and any personal-portfolio data from this system entirely — the judge panel operates only on public-company filings and market data, never on the owner's positions, per CLAUDE.md §11.

All judge, aggregator, and devil's-advocate sub-agent calls run on Sonnet per the repo's model policy (CLAUDE.md §1.7) — never the orchestrator's top model — with reasoning effort set high for the devil's-advocate and adversarial stages, low/medium for mechanical extraction stages.

Pin the exact judge model version used for backtest calibration and re-validate (do not silently reuse old calibration weights) whenever the underlying model updates, mirroring the edge-detection-method.md discipline of freezing the model and treating refits as a rare, explicit, logged action.

backtest_protocol: Historical universe: build TWO cohorts, not one — (a) winners: extend the existing scripts/bumper/study.py population, restricted to quantum/physical-AI/robotics/AI-infra industries, using its existing >=5x/5y or >=3x/3y run-detection logic; (b) failures: a new scripts/bumper/graveyard.py module carrying the named collapsed cohort from the brief (NKLA, RIDE, GOEV, Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, Hyliion, RGTI/ARQQ post-SPAC quantum names, MicroVision, SoundHound, BigBear.ai, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Virgin Galactic, Momentus) run through the identical feature/judge pipeline. This closes the gap the brief itself flags: the current study's winner list has no failed-name counterexample to test against, so its AUCs cannot yet be trusted as discriminating rather than merely descriptive of survivors.

Dates: freeze every feature and every judge's candidate filing set at run-start-minus-3-months (mirroring study.py's existing asof convention), using each filing's SEC EDGAR acceptance timestamp as the cutoff — never today's restated data or a filing dated after the frozen point. For graveyard names, 'run start' is defined as the date the eventual-collapse narrative first went mainstream (SPAC-merger close, first bullish analyst re-rate, or IPO date), so the judge is scored on exactly what a live screen would have had in hand, never on post-collapse disclosures.

Leakage avoidance: (1) freeze the judge rubric, prompts, and the aggregator's weight-calibration method before touching the held-out test era — no rubric iteration once test-era events are scored, mirroring edge-detection-method.md's 'freeze the model' rule; (2) calibrate aggregator weights only on a train-era slice (e.g. 2015-2021 vintage events), evaluate on a held-out era never touched during rubric design (e.g. 2022-2026 vintage); (3) hard-gate every judge's EDGAR retrieval call by the frozen as-of date so no filing dated after it can enter context; (4) build each quarter's candidate list from the mechanical universe filter applied blind to outcome, never by hand-picking known winners or known failures into the test set.

Count independent EVENTS, not filing-rows (edge-detection-method.md section 4): the unit is one company run-episode (winner) or one company collapse-episode (failure), not each quarterly filing inside it. Where a company has multiple candidate windows (e.g. a name that both spiked and later collapsed), treat each episode as a separate event and check they are not contiguous/overlapping before counting them as independent; report the actual count of independent episodes used, not the row count in the underlying dataframe.

Gate 1 — Separation: bootstrap the aggregator's calibrated probability band against actual outcome (did the name go on to a >=3-5x re-rate / recognized sector-leader status within the horizon, or collapse/delist) across all independent events, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across every judge and every feature tested (not a favorable subset) — report the corrected p-values, not just the raw ones.

Gate 2 — Fast detection: verify the judge panel's score, computed only from filings available at run-start-minus-3-months, agrees directionionally with the retrospective (full-hindsight) label within a lag l* measured in filing-cycles; if l* exceeds the horizon being screened for (i.e., the panel can only tell winners from failures after the fact), the system fails this gate and is not deployable regardless of Gate 1.

Gate 3 — Edge survival: compute rho = (online, causal-only judge score's discriminative power) / (retrospective, full-hindsight judge score's discriminative power) across the held-out era; require rho >= 0.7 per edge-detection-method.md's threshold, and treat rho in [0.5, 0.7) as a warning that most of the apparent edge is hindsight rather than a signal that would have fired live.

Era test: split events by listing/run-start vintage into at least three regimes — pre-2022 (low-rate, pre-AI-capex-boom), 2022-2023 (rate-hike drawdown, the SPAC-bust graveyard's dominant era), and 2024-2026 (AI-capex boom) — and report Gate 1-3 results PER ERA, not only pooled. A panel that only passes the gates in the 2024-2026 era is regime-fitted to the current AI cycle, not a genuine discriminator, and must be reported as such rather than deployed on that basis.

Adversarial review: dispatch a dedicated devil's-advocate sub-agent (superpowers:requesting-code-review / systematic-debugging), briefed only to find look-ahead leakage, multiple-testing inflation, and event double-counting in the backtest code and data, given full access to the code and data and asked for empirical demonstrations (re-run a suspect step, show the number) rather than opinions; record the number of rubric/weighting variants tried before arriving at the reported result, since that count is the denominator of any significance claim per edge-detection-method.md section 8.

Costs/cash/tax/wrapper: not directly applicable to a screening system (it does not size or execute trades), but report what the SHORTLISTING cost would have been in practice — filing-reading token/compute cost per candidate at the panel's actual model pricing, and the false-positive rate's implied cost of wasted deep-dive research time — as the closest analogue to edge-detection-method.md's final accounting-that-changes-conclusions step for a research (not trading) system.
proposals.expected_base_rate_and_payoff: Base rate is low and the payoff is extreme right-tail-skewed, per the base rates the brief already opened and verified from Ritter's IPO dataset and Bessembinder (2018): unprofitable-at-IPO issuers averaged -30.7% market-adjusted over 3 years (n=3,926, 1980-2024); across all IPOs 1975-2021, only ~15.7% exceeded +100% and only ~1.7% exceeded +500% over 3 years — the 'bumper' outcome is a thin right tail of the pre-profit universe, not a typical outcome, and the best-performing ~4% of all listed US stocks account for essentially the entire market's lifetime wealth creation above T-bills (Bessembinder). Applying this to the target universe (pre-profit small caps in quantum/physical-AI/AI-infra), a reasonable prior for "becomes a recognized sector leader within ~24 months" for an unscreened name in this bucket sits in the low single digits (roughly 1-5%, inferred by combining the IPO/deSPAC base rates above with the sector's currently elevated but historically volatile re-rating frequency — this composite figure is inferred, not independently re-derived this session, and should be replaced with the graveyard-vs-winner event count once scripts/bumper/graveyard.py exists). Given every signal family reviewed here is rated "supporting" at best (near-coin-flip AUCs of 0.5-0.61 in the target population, several features actually inverted below 0.5), the honest expectation is that this system delivers a MODEST lift, not a strong edge: a realistic target is moving the probability band for shortlisted, panel-approved names to roughly 2-4x the unscreened base rate (e.g., ~5-15% rather than ~1-5%), not a high-confidence pick. The devil's-advocate gate and hard-override exclusions (going-concern, delinquent filings) are expected to do more of the real work — cutting the worst false positives — than the positive score is expected to do at finding true positives, consistent with the graveyard discriminators reading as much stronger filters than any of the bullish signal families. Payoff profile if it works: a small number of very large winners (consistent with Bessembinder's skew) funding many near-zero or modest-loss outcomes on the rest of the shortlist — meaning this system's honest use case is a portfolio-construction input (size many small positions across the shortlist, expect most near-flat-to-down, rely on the tail) rather than a single-name conviction tool, and its calibration must be re-validated against a genuinely held-out era before any of these numbers are treated as more than an untested design target.
build_plan_first_two_weeks: Day 1: superpowers:brainstorming pass on the panel architecture and rubric wording (owner-required before any new build per CLAUDE.md section 1); write the spec via superpowers:writing-plans, naming every module below explicitly so the plan is executable without re-deriving scope.

Day 2: extend the data layer for the failure cohort — new scripts/bumper/graveyard.py (mirrors scripts/bumper/sources.py's cache_json/companyfacts/quarterly_series helpers) carrying the named collapsed tickers and their run-start/collapse dates; wire it into scripts/bumper/study.py's existing feature pipeline so winners and failures are computed identically. superpowers:test-driven-development: write the graveyard-feature test before the fetch code.

Day 3-4: new scripts/aiinvest/edgar_fts.py (EDGAR full-text-search wrapper, extending the existing scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py submissions/companyfacts primitives) for the anchor-customer, capacity, and going-concern flag pulls; new scripts/aiinvest/form4.py to parse Form 4 XML transaction codes/shares/price per CIK (the data_gaps list confirms no parser exists yet). TDD each against fixture filings (a real RIDE pre-order 8-K vs. a bona fide binding contract 8-K) asserting the flag extraction tells them apart at the text level before any judge sees them.

Day 5: build the shortlist/screen module scripts/bumper/screen.py that assembles the quant feature vector (features.py) + raw flags (edgar_fts.py, form4.py) into the ~20-50 name/quarter candidate list, with the going-concern/delinquent-filing hard-override routing names OUT of the queue at this stage, before any judge is invoked (cost control — never send an auto-rejected name to the panel).

Day 6-7: build scripts/bumper/judges/ as one module per judge (contract_reality.py, dilution_runway.py, insider_conviction.py, narrative_delivery.py, sector_timing.py), each a thin Sonnet sub-agent wrapper (model:'sonnet' per CLAUDE.md section 1.7) taking the filing set + rubric text and returning a strict JSON score+citation schema; TDD with the same fixture filings from Day 3-4 plus a known-winner/known-failure pair per judge, asserting the rubric score separates them in the expected direction before trusting any live output.

Day 8: build scripts/bumper/devils_advocate.py (a Sonnet sub-agent briefed only on the graveyard_discriminators list, run against the same filing set) and scripts/bumper/aggregate.py (calibrated blend + hard-override gate + abstain logic), producing the final probability-band + top-3-reasons + counter-argument output schema.

Day 9-10: implement the validation harness scripts/bumper/validate.py per edge-detection-method.md — bootstrap+BH-FDR separation test, fast-detection lag check, edge-survival ratio (rho), and the era-split reporting (pre-2022 / 2022-2023 / 2024-2026) — run it end-to-end against the combined winner+graveyard cohort from Day 2 before claiming any result.

Throughout both weeks: invoke superpowers:verification-before-completion before reporting any judge or backtest result — show the actual extracted filing citations, judge scores, and validate.py gate outputs, never an assertion that it works; the orchestrator (main agent) alone stays on the top model at max effort per CLAUDE.md section 1.7 — every module above that calls an LLM runs on Sonnet.
risks: Survivorship bias is not yet closed: until scripts/bumper/graveyard.py exists and is run through the identical pipeline, every AUC and every judge-rubric validation in this design is untested against real failures — treat all current numbers (from the brief) as descriptive of survivors only, not yet as a validated discriminator.

The quant screen's own signal is weak-to-inverted in the target population (AUC 0.5-0.61, several features below 0.5) — if the judge panel cannot demonstrably add lift BEYOND this near-random screen, the whole system reduces to expensive filing-reading that repackages noise; the backtest's Gate 1-3 must show the PANEL's lift specifically, not just that panel-approved names happened to include some past winners.

LLM judge hallucination/miscitation: a judge fabricating or misreading a filing citation is a correctness failure with compliance consequences (a fabricated 'binding contract confirmed' claim on a real ticker); the citation-dereference verification guardrail must actually fetch and match the cited language before any claim is kept, not merely require a citation be present.

Independent-event count is likely small (per edge-detection-method.md section 4, this repo's own prior work found ~10 independent episodes inside 134 'significant' days) — with a plausible 10-30 independent events per era across quantum/physical-AI/AI-infra collapses and winners combined, statistical power for the separation and era tests is thin, and calibration weights fit on that few events risk overfitting; report the exact event count with every result, not just p-values.

Regime dependence: quantum/physical-AI/AI-infra 2024-2026 is a single hot capital cycle (per the brief's own base-rate section on tech-IPO outperformance being era-specific); a panel validated only inside this era is regime-fitted, not structurally sound — the era-test requirement in the backtest protocol is the mitigation, but it depends on the graveyard cohort actually spanning a colder era (2022-2023 rate-hike bust), which it does (Virgin Orbit, Astra, Lordstown, Canoo all collapsed in that window).

Cost/latency at scale: five Sonnet judges plus a devil's-advocate reading full 10-Ks/8-Ks per candidate is compute- and token-expensive; without the hard quant/flag-based shortlist cap (~20-50 names/quarter), this does not scale to the full ~500-1000 name universe — the shortlist step is load-bearing for cost, not just for signal.

Compliance/liability: a calibrated 'probability of becoming a sector leader' attached to a real, named, pre-profit ticker is easy to misread as a buy signal despite every guardrail; mitigate with the mandatory disclaimer, no position-sizing output, no order-placement capability anywhere in this design, and explicit educational-research framing on every output, per this repo's CLAUDE.md sections 1 and 8 and the owner's IBKR-data hard rule (section 11) which this system's scope never touches.

Data-gap dependencies: the Insider Conviction judge needs a working Form 4 parser and the Sector Timing/Narrative judges benefit from hiring-velocity and patent-claim-quality data that the repo's own data_gaps list confirms do not exist yet (no free real-time institutional order flow, no working StockTwits/Reddit access this session, no in-house hiring-velocity scraper) — judges should ABSTAIN on those specific rubric lines rather than silently score without the input, and the build plan should not overpromise coverage those modules don't yet have.

Model/version drift: Sonnet updates between backtest calibration and live deployment can silently shift judge scoring distributions; per edge-detection-method.md's 'freeze the model, refitting is the silent killer' principle, pin the exact model version used for calibration and require an explicit, logged re-validation pass (not a silent reuse of old weights) on any model update.

scores.proposal: P1 — "Bumper Radar — Evidence-First Pre-Rerating Screener" (disqualification-first, single scorer + single narrating judge)
scores.critique: This is the only one of the three that actually obeys the brief's headline finding — core_families is empty, the graveyard discriminators are the one category with real case-level separation, everything else is a capped supporting signal — and it builds the architecture around that fact instead of around a favorite feature. Its thesis line says it explicitly: 'the honest design is a disqualification-first screener.' The backtest protocol is a near-literal implementation of references/edge-detection-method.md's own gate order (verified: the doc's ASCII pipeline near the top matches this proposal's Gate1/2/3 + era-test structure almost clause for clause), including the leakage items the method doc calls the 'silent killer' (freeze-then-test, point-in-time SIC/XBRL only, label locked before scoring). Buildability is genuinely the strongest of the three: gates.py is pure-function, unit-testable exactly like the already-shipped scripts/bumper/features.py (verified: features.py already has auc(), runway_years, shares_growth_yoy, run_start() — the empirical AUCs quoted in the brief visibly come from this exact module), the judge is a single Sonnet call rather than an orchestration of five, and the scorer/judge separation (judge narrates and flags, never overrides the number) is a good, cheap guardrail against LLM narrative-smoothing. Weakest point: the build plan reinvents a 'universe.py' point-in-time builder without explicitly citing the already-working scripts/bumper/study.py + sources.py it should extend instead — minor redundancy risk, not a design flaw. It also, like the others, still needs a from-scratch EDGAR full-text-search wrapper and Form-4 parser (verified: grep of scripts/aiinvest/edgar.py shows only submissions/companyfacts helpers, no efts.sec.gov call; no form4.py exists anywhere in the repo) — that's real but modest net-new work, not a two-week blocker.

scores.proposal: P2 — "Bumper Radar" (capital-web economic-link-gain as primary trigger)
scores.critique: Weakest of the three, and the flaw is structural, not cosmetic. The brief hands the designers core_families: [] — no signal cleared the bar — and this proposal answers by naming capital_web_edge_gain 'core / primary trigger' anyway, with zero AUC or empirical backing for that specific feature (unlike shares_growth_yoy's measured 0.61, this signal was never tested against anything). Its own risk section then concedes the exact reason it shouldn't be core: the capital-web graph (verified: scripts/aiinvest/capital_web.py is a static, hand-curated EDGES list with real types equity_stake/compute_commitment/customer/voting_power/subsidiary/infra_partner as of a single 2026-05 snapshot — no versioning, no diff history) was 'never built with graveyard failures as nodes,' so scoring off its diff is survivorship bias baked into the data source itself, not just the sample. That is a self-inflicted wound the other two proposals avoid by keeping economic-link/anchor-customer signals as gated triage flags rather than the primary trigger. Falsifiability is fine on paper (same three gates, same era test) but the proposal's own build plan admits the riskiest, most time-consuming step — hand-building a point-in-time graph-diff fixture for 30-45 names — eats days 9-11 of a 14-day plan, which is a real threat to actually finishing rather than a hypothetical one. Buildability is capped by the fact that no snapshot/diff mechanism for capital_web.py exists today (confirmed) and would need to be built from a standing start, on top of the same EDGAR full-text-search and Form-4 gaps every proposal shares.

scores.proposal: P3 — "Bumper Radar: Judge-Panel Screen" (5 narrow Sonnet judges + calibrated aggregator + mandatory devil's-advocate)
scores.critique: Second-best on substance and arguably the most honest about the brief's central gap: it is the only proposal that puts building the failed-name counterexample cohort (graveyard.py, run through the identical pipeline as the winners) as an explicit, named Day-2 deliverable rather than an assumption, which directly answers the brief's own complaint that revenue_inflection and capex_or_capacity have no failed-name test set. Its falsifiability design matches P1's rigor (same three gates, same era split, same freeze-the-rubric-before-test-era discipline) and adds a genuinely good idea neither other proposal has as a hard mechanical step: verification must dereference and re-fetch every cited filing before a judge's claim is kept, not just require a citation be present — a concrete defense against exactly the narrative-smoothing risk it names for itself. Where it loses points is buildability: five separate judge modules plus a devil's-advocate plus an isotonic/logistic-calibrated aggregator plus graveyard.py plus a Form-4 parser plus a new EDGAR full-text-search wrapper, in two weeks, by one developer, is a materially larger build surface than P1's single-scorer-plus-single-judge design — and the proposal's own risk list flags this cost/latency problem itself ('five Sonnet judges... is compute- and token-expensive'). This reads like a strong v2 once P1's simpler skeleton is proven, not a realistic v1.

judges.winner: P1 — "Bumper Radar — Evidence-First Pre-Rerating Screener for Pre-Profit Emerging-Sector Small Caps" (the disqualification-first design, single deterministic scorer + single narrating-only judge). It is the only proposal whose architecture is a direct consequence of the brief's own finding (core_families is empty; the graveyard discriminators are the one evidence category with real separation) rather than a design built first and rationalized against the evidence second, its backtest protocol most closely and completely implements references/edge-detection-method.md's actual gate order, and it has the smallest, most reusable build surface (leans directly on the already-shipped, already-unit-tested scripts/bumper/features.py + study.py AUC machinery) for a one-developer two-week build.
graft_from_others: From P2: keep the capital-web (capital_web.py / quantum_capital_web.py / physical_ai_capital_web.py) edge-diff as a free triage trigger — which handful of names get the expensive filing-gate treatment first — never as a scored signal. This is cheap (the graph already exists) and doesn't inherit P2's survivorship problem because it's advisory, not evidentiary.

From P3: adopt the mandatory devil's-advocate pass as a hard pre-verdict gate — a second, cheap Sonnet call briefed only on the graveyard discriminators to argue the bear case — before P1's single judge finalizes a band. P1's current design has no adversarial check on its own narrator.

From P3: adopt the citation-dereference verification step literally — actually fetch and confirm each cited filing contains the claimed language before keeping the claim in a judge's output, rather than merely requiring a citation be present.

From P3: adopt the concrete, ready-to-use graveyard ticker list (NKLA, RIDE, GOEV, Lordstown, Canoo, Arrival, Hyliion, MicroVision, BigBear.ai, Velodyne, Luminar, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Virgin Galactic, Momentus) and the explicit 'build TWO cohorts through the identical pipeline' step as the literal backtest fixture for P1's Gate 1-3 harness — P1 gestures at this cohort but P3 names it concretely and ties it to a build-order (Day 2) that closes the brief's stated gap fastest.

scores.proposal: Design A — "Bumper Radar — Evidence-First Pre-Rerating Screener" (deterministic gates.py/scorer.py, judge narrates-only, never overrides)
scores.critique: Verified this session: the brief's own AUC numbers (rev_growth_yoy tech_small=0.509, rev_acceleration tech_small=0.483, shares_growth_yoy all=0.611) match data/bumper/2026-09-25/separation_matched.json almost exactly — this design's thesis ('no core signal validated, disqualification-first') is the honest reading of real output, not a rhetorical hedge. It correctly identifies the graveyard discriminators (going-concern, runway-compression-rate not level, governance self-dealing, exchange-compliance, funding-gap departures) as the only category with real case-level separating power and architects around that: hard gates cap the score, supporting signals are weight-capped by measured AUC, and the judge narrates/flags but structurally cannot override the number — the cleanest defense of the three against LLM-judge narrative inflation. Falsifiability protocol correctly implements edge-detection-method.md's gates (separation/fast-detection/edge-survival, BH-FDR, event clustering, era splits), but the backtest cohort is winners+graveyard ONLY — no neutral 'ran neither way' sample — so it selects on outcome extremes exactly as it warns against for the revenue_inflection family; it doesn't catch its own version of that flaw. Buildability: plans scripts/aiinvest/universe.py, gates.py, form4.py, scorer.py, backtest/ from scratch, entirely ignoring scripts/bumper/{sources.py,features.py,study.py} — verified to already exist and to be the actual module that produced the cited AUCs (cache_json/companyfacts/quarterly_series helpers, confirmed by reading the files). Building a parallel pipeline under aiinvest/ instead of extending the real bumper module is wasted motion for a 2-week/1-developer budget; edgar.py also has no full-text-search wrapper and no form4 parser yet, so gates.py/form4.py are genuinely greenfield.

scores.proposal: Design B — "Bumper Radar" (capital-web-edge-gain as primary trigger, single narrator judge)
scores.critique: Structural flaw verified this session: scripts/aiinvest/capital_web.py's EDGES list is a static, hand-curated dict stamped 'as_of 2026-05' with certainty tags but no timestamped edge-gain history — it is not a time series, so capital_web_edge_gain (the design's own 'primary trigger, core' signal) has zero measured AUC and can't be diffed against a prior snapshot that doesn't exist yet. The design promotes the single least-evidenced signal in the whole packet to primary status while relegating the one signal with real measured separation (shares_growth_yoy, AUC 0.61) to 'supporting' — an inversion of the evidence the study actually produced. Its own risk section admits this ('the graph is manually curated and stale-by-construction... expect rho materially below 1') and flags the point-in-time backtest fixture as 'the single highest-risk, most time-consuming step' — an honest tell the core mechanism may not be testable in two weeks. Its best contribution is methodological, not architectural: it's the only one of the three that explicitly names a THIRD, neutral cohort ('names that neither ran nor collapsed') in the backtest, correctly diagnosing that omitting it 'selects on outcome' — the exact gap both A and C have and don't catch. Buildability gets real credit for reusing verified-existing modules correctly (capital_web.py, physical_ai_capital_web.py, quantum_capital_web.py, and news_graph.py's detect_candidate_edges/classify_certainty, confirmed present by grep), but the hardest, highest-value piece of the plan — hand-reconstructing historical, as-filed-date capital-web edges for ~30-45 tickers — is a hand-curation task, not a script, and is unlikely to close in two weeks solo.

scores.proposal: Design C — "Bumper Radar: Judge-Panel Screen" (5 narrow LLM judges + devil's-advocate + calibrated aggregator)
scores.critique: Same well-grounded signal table and AUC citations as Design A, plus it is the only one of the three that explicitly sets out to close the brief's flagged gap ('no failed-name counterexample') by building a matching scripts/bumper/graveyard.py cohort run through the identical pipeline — and it is the only design that correctly names and reuses the REAL existing scripts/bumper/study.py/sources.py helpers (cache_json, companyfacts, quarterly_series — all verified present by reading the files) rather than inventing a parallel pipeline. Falsifiability is solid (same three-gate protocol, BH-FDR, event-count discipline, era test) and its per-judge fixture testing ('assert score separates a known winner/failure pair before trusting live output') is a clean, testable pattern — but like Design A it uses only two cohorts (winners+failures), missing the neutral sample Design B correctly flags as the standard way this kind of study fools itself, and five judges scoring in parallel materially inflates the multiple-testing denominator the design's own risk section admits needs tracking. Buildability is the weakest of the three in a 2-week/1-developer budget despite the good scripts/bumper/ reuse: the plan requires roughly 11 new modules (graveyard.py, screen.py, edgar_fts.py, form4.py, five separate judge wrappers, devils_advocate.py, aggregate.py, validate.py) plus prompt calibration for each judge and a cost-control shortlist gate to keep 5-Sonnet-judges-per-candidate affordable — a materially larger build surface than either single-scorer design, for a system whose own guardrails admit the aggregator's calibration is fit on a 'small-n' (~20-40 independent episode) set.

judges.winner: Design A — "Bumper Radar — Evidence-First Pre-Rerating Screener for Pre-Profit Emerging-Sector Small Caps" (deterministic gates.py/scorer.py; judge narrates, never overrides the number)
graft_from_others: From Design B: add the third, neutral cohort ('pre-profit sector small caps that neither ran nor collapsed') to A's backtest_protocol — without it, A's own winners+graveyard-only comparison selects on outcome extremes, the exact failure mode A calls out for the brief's revenue_inflection family.

From Design B: treat capital_web.py/physical_ai_capital_web.py/quantum_capital_web.py edges and news_graph.py's classify_certainty (filed/reported/rumored) as an INPUT FEED into A's binding-demand gate, not a standalone trigger — cheap to wire in since both modules already exist, and it gives A's anchor-customer check a certainty ladder for free.

From Design C: build A's universe.py/gates.py/scorer.py as extensions of the REAL scripts/bumper/{sources.py,features.py,study.py} module (cache_json/companyfacts/quarterly_series helpers, verified present) instead of a fresh scripts/aiinvest/ pipeline — the single highest-leverage change to A's build plan, and it directly fixes A's weakest score (buildability).

From Design C: adopt the graveyard.py failed-cohort module and the 'assert the gate/score separates a known winner/failure fixture pair before trusting live output' TDD pattern for each of A's gate functions.

From Design C: adopt the mandatory devil's-advocate adversarial pass (a separate Sonnet sub-agent briefed only on the graveyard discriminators, run before any verdict finalizes) as a check on A's judge output — it catches cases where the deterministic score itself missed a qualitative red flag no gate encodes yet.

From Design C: the Contract Reality judge's specific rule — an announced deal only counts once a SUBSEQUENT filing shows delivered units/recognized revenue/growing RPO, not on the announcement alone — is a good concrete tightening of A's own binding-demand gate description.
